articles.title: 'I’ve already thought about it' Joao Felix vows to be the one to assist Cristiano Ronaldo’s historic 1,000th goal
articles.summary: Joao Felix expresses his desire to be the one to assist Cristiano Ronaldo in reaching his historic 1,000th career goal. As Ronaldo nears this monumental milestone, Felix reflects on their shared experiences and his goals with Al-Nassr.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo is closing in on 1,000 career goals, but one of his Portugal and Al-Nassr teammates has already thought about how he would like the landmark moment to happen. Joao Felix has admitted that he wants to be the player who provides the assist for Ronaldo's historic strike, having shared the pitch with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner at both club and international level.Ronaldo has scored 979 goals for club and country, leaving him 21 short of the 1,000-goal mark. A VAR check denied him what would have been his 980th goal during Portugal's recent victory over Wales, meaning the wait for one of football's most remarkable individual milestones continues.Felix, meanwhile, has made no secret of the fact that he would love to play a direct part in the moment, and he has already imagined what he would do if Ronaldo reaches the final goal with him on the pitch.Felix has already imagined Ronaldo's 1,000th goalSpeaking to AS in an interview carried by A Bola, Felix was asked about the possibility of helping Ronaldo reach the landmark, and his answer suggested that the scenario has already crossed his mind."I've already thought about it," Felix said."When he has one goal left, I'll see if I can provide the assist for him. That goal will remain in the history of football, and to contribute to it would be a wonderful moment."Ronaldo's pursuit of 1,000 goals has become one of the defining individual storylines of his later career, with the 41-year-old continuing to add to a tally that has already passed 900 despite being well beyond the age at which most elite forwards have retired.Felix is becoming an important figure alongside RonaldoFelix is not simply a teammate waiting for the opportunity to create Ronaldo's milestone. The Portugal international is enjoying an increasingly productive period of his own since moving to Saudi Arabia, where he has established himself as an important player for Al-Nassr.The former Atletico Madrid and Chelsea forward was named the best player in Al-Nassr's recent league title triumph and believes his move to Saudi Arabia in the summer of 2025 has helped him reach another level of maturity.Felix has registered 30 goals and 22 assists in 55 appearances across all competitions for the club.His contribution also helped Al-Nassr finally secure the Saudi Arabian title, something that Felix described as particularly special because of what it meant to Ronaldo, who had been pursuing the league championship since arriving in Saudi Arabia.That shared experience has given Felix another reason to appreciate the opportunity of playing alongside Ronaldo, both at club level and with Portugal."It's something few people in football can say they've done, playing with him on the national team and at club level. It's an honor," Felix said."We grew up seeing Cristiano as our idol, a role model, and now I can share moments with him."Ronaldo's chase continues with Portugal and Al-NassrRonaldo has already made seven appearances for Al-Nassr across all competitions this season, scoring three goals, and he will have further opportunities to reduce the 21-goal gap as the campaign progresses.He was also involved as Portugal began their Nations League campaign, with Jorge Jesus' side beating Wales 1-0 thanks to a decisive goal from Felix.Portugal are competing in League A Group 4 and have a demanding international schedule ahead, with a trip to face Denmark on October 1 followed by another meeting with Norway on October 4.The immediate focus remains on winning those matches, but Ronaldo's personal pursuit will continue to follow him into every game.At 979 goals, the target is close enough for teammates to think about what the eventual 1,000th might look like. Felix has already decided what his preferred role would be: having the ball at the right moment, seeing Ronaldo's run and supplying the pass that could become part of football history.For now, though, Ronaldo still has 21 goals to find.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s $1.4 billion fortune gets another boost as football legend acquires 25% stake in Spanish club
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, the football legend, has been known for his talent on the field for over the last two decades.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo, the football legend, has been known for his talent on the field for over the last two decades. While the Portuguese star player is easily one of the most talented athletes in the world, he has also been pretty business oriented. One of Cristiano Ronaldo’s profitable investments have turned heads in the last few months.Cristiano Ronaldo buys a 25% stake in a Spanish second division club amid his profitable venturesA few months ago, the Portuguese legend Cristiano Ronaldo ended up acquiring a 25% stake in the Spanish second division club UD Almeria.As per reports, it has not been confirmed how much the deal cost but it was done through the Portugal captain's CR7 Sports Investments company, and is reported to be a long term strategic investment from Cristiano Ronaldo.In a statement, the star football player Cristiano Ronaldo weighed in on his investment as he said, "I have long had the ambition to contribute to football beyond the pitch,...UD Almería is a Spanish club with a strong foundation and clear growth potential. I wish to work with the team leading the club to support it in its new phase of growth."Spanish second division club UD Almeria’s coach Juan Francesc Ferrer 'Rubi' also weighed in on Cristiano Ronaldo becoming a stakeholder in the team as he said, "From our perspective, we're very happy…Of course, we welcome him. I think it's great news because someone like him, with his extensive knowledge of sport and football, can really help a club like ours”Spanish second division club UD Almeria’s coach Juan Francesc Ferrer 'Rubi' added, "It's very exciting for the whole club, the city, and the province. Everyone knows the good relationship Cristiano has with the owners. "You find out things as they happen, but I don't think it's important when I found out or not. The important thing is that he's arrived here to join us [as a shareholder]. We're very happy."In an official statement, the team wrote, “Cristiano Ronaldo has acquired 25% of UD Almería’s shares through CR7 Sports Investments, a subsidiary of CR7 S.A., marking an important step in the continued expansion of both the club and the Portuguese entrepreneur’s investment portfolio.”Cristiano Ronald remains strategic with his investments as he nears retirementAs per Forbes, Cristiano Ronaldo’s private investment portfolio and brand equity are valued between $850 million and $900 million, contributing to an overall estimated net worth of $1.4 billionWhile the star player has been a force to be reckoned with on the field for the last two decades, it seems he is getting more strategic with his wealth.Though he has hinted at retiring, nothing has been confirmed yet.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sponsorship: Is Anybody Going To Front Up?
articles.summary: With the club without a front of shirt deal, Roker Report asks whether anybody is going to step forward and sponsor the Cats…
articles.body:
The first international break of a new season is often a good time to sit back and take stock of how things are shaping up.

At Sunderland things are shaping up pretty well – the new players appear to be settling in and performances have been encouraging, yet there is something out there on the pitch that doesn't look quite as it should, and whilst it doesn't have a direct impact on results, the long-term consequences would still be best avoided.

For the first time since 1983-84 Sunderland do not have a front of shirt sponsor and whilst that might not be an issue for the traditionalists it is peculiar that a club trying to maximise revenue so that it can compete at the top has allowed itself to so far miss out on a potentially massive source of income.

The 2026-27 kit designs look good enough as they are without having to carry cluttered logos and this might prove to be a boost in terms of retail sales at least, but advertising remains one of the biggest money makers in football and not having a 'major partner' leaves a big gap to fill on the balance sheet.

This is of course a lot more palatable to the supporters than having to stomach the sight of the Lads or Lasses running out and legitimising some sort of dubious organisation or group. In the summer when there were strong rumours that Visit Ghana was to link up with Sunderland, there were legitimate concerns raised about what message that would send to members of the fanbase and the wider world.

Whilst it is not known exactly why that deal fell through it would be nice to think that the delay in now selecting a replacement is in part due to the hierarchy becoming more circumspect in their negotiations.

The big problem however is that morals and sticking to a social conscious doesn't always help pay the bills. There has always been an uneasy relationship between sponsorship and sport, a necessarily evil if you will, but one that fans can overlook if it doesn't get too awkward.

Acting as walking billboards just because you want to show your colours can feel somewhat exploitive at the best of times, but given the global nature of the Premier League and Football League, plus the current economic climate, we aren't even promoting local or national brands anymore. Pushing unconnected services, or industries that can be damaging to society, is disagreeable to many, yet it is a difficult square to circle because there are few 'acceptable' firms out there that can afford to join the party.

Had something with Visit Ghan a been signed off Sunderland were set to bank a record price. Now that is off the table the pool of suitably monied options is even smaller, especially so since gambling groups are no longer authorised on the front of shirts, and that makes filling the vacation even harder.

It is easy for me to insist that the club balances image with income, but actually achieving that does not appear straightforward given the constraints. For instance, on a purely personal note, I was disappointed that a crypto casino had been brought in as sleeve sponsor, but then nearly a third of all Premier League clubs have such arrangements so it must be hard for the executives to turn their noses up at the cash being put down.

On that note, banning gambling from the front of shirts but still allowing it on sleeves does seem ill-conceived to me anyway, but its presence in any form is another anomaly in the bigger debate – who is the arbiter in what type of business model is deemed acceptable or ethical in the first place?

There will be a line somewhere, but it may shift from person to person, and, if we are being honest, could move again depending on the results the players wearing the branding are producing, which are often the biggest determinator in some peoples minds as to whether a revenue stream is tolerable.

From a business point of view, it is understandable why you would want to get into bed with SAFC right now. High profile games, such as a Saturday night prime time fixture with reigning champions Arsenal , or a hugely anticipated return to European action, bring lots of attention to Wearside and with it plenty of possible customers.

UEFA rules might complicate discussions as their own rules on who or what can be worn on a strip are fairly strict, but in theory the Lads are the more marketable than ever. There have been enough smaller relationships struck up lately to support that to, so it is not as if the commercial representatives have been sat on their hands doing nothing.

In August there was a suggestion that Nissan had become an official club partner, although they are not currently listed as one on the official website, but Seriös Group have definitely agreed to a new multi-year agreement whilst P1 Travel came on board recently too.

The Lasses have also secured some backing of late, as this month Elliott James (EJ Legal) was announced as the new back of shorts sponsor for 2026-27, going alongside Everyone Active, a regular collaborator, who are now their 'Official Training Wear Partner'. It is the search for a main tie up that appears to have cooled down though, so when it happens, and who it is with, is intriguing.

We are led to believe that discussions are ongoing behind the scenes, and that the club is still expecting any deal to have a high valuation; it is promising that Sunderland does not want to sell itself short, but there is little else to go on for the time being.

As with transfers, there are few rumours emanating from the Stadium of Light, but then again recruitment been a strong point for some time now and is setting the standard that all other aspects of the club are being judged by.

If that is to remain the case, and Florent Ghisolfi is to have the spending power needed going forward, the kitty could do with the extra boost a front of shirt partner would bring, and for that reason alone the sooner something is confirmed the better.

articles.title: Week 3 was huge for 49ers in hunt for NFC West crown
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers got a much-needed cushion in the NFC West during Week 3 action. Here are the updated standings.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers ' Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals took on a little extra importance Sunday evening when the Denver Broncos held off the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football.

Denver's 34-30 victory capped off a terrific day for the 49ers that saw every other team in the NFC West lose.

First, the Seattle Seahawks fell to the Washington Commanders 33-31 in the early slate for their first loss of the year. The 49ers handled business at home vs. the Cardinals to continue their undefeated season in the afternoon. Then in the nightcap the Rams joined the Cardinals among the two-loss teams in the division.

Here's what the NFC West standings look like after Week 3:

This doesn't mean much at this point since we're only one-sixth of the way through the year. However, the 49ers are 2-0 inside the division and they've now given themselves a one-game cushion on the Seahawks and a two-game cushion on the Rams. Given the injury problems they've had this season an extra game or two of wiggle room it what promises to be a tough divisional race down the stretch could be the difference between winning the division and not.

There's a long way to go for the 49ers, but it's hard to ask for a better third week of the season than the one San Francisco got.

articles.body:
France will take on Belgium in their second UEFA Nations League fixture on Monday at the Stade Roi Baudouin, aiming to make it two wins from two in the competition.

Les Bleus continue to be regarded as one of Europe's leading international teams, even as they begin a new era under manager Zinedine Zidane. France opened their Group A1 campaign with a controlled 1-0 victory over Türkiye, giving them an ideal start. Their latest major tournament run also saw them reach the semi-finals of the 2026 World Cup, where they were eventually eliminated by Spain , who went on to lift the trophy. France will also take confidence from their excellent record against Belgium, having won each of their last five meetings over the past decade.

France will have to cope without captain Kylian Mbappé for this important encounter. The forward hyperextended his left knee soon after scoring the winning goal against Türkiye and has since returned to Madrid to continue his rehabilitation.

His absence means Zidane is expected to make changes to the attacking setup. Ousmane Dembélé could move into the central striker role, with Michael Olise and Désiré Doué likely to operate on either side of him in a youthful and energetic front three.

The midfield is expected to feature Manu Koné, Adrien Rabiot , and Rayan Cherki , combining strength, creativity, and attacking intent.

Mike Maignan should continue in goal, while Dayot Upamecano and Maxence Lacroix are tipped to start at the heart of the defence.

Jules Koundé and Adrien Truffert are expected to occupy the fullback positions, giving France additional protection against Belgium's wide threat.

Possible France starting XI: Maignan ; Kounde, Upamecano, Lacroix, Truffert; Cherki, Kone, Rabiot; Olise, Dembele, Doue

articles.body:
Turkey and Italy will face each other in their next UEFA Nations League encounter on Monday at the Matli Stadyumu Atatürk Spor Kompleksi as both teams will look to come back to winning ways after their opening loss.

Turkey vs Italy – Match preview and team news

Venue: Matli Stadyumu Atatürk Spor Kompleksi, Bursa.

Altay Bayındır is set to start for Türkiye as regular first-choice keeper Uğurcan Çakır serves a suspension following his red card against France .

Head coach Vincenzo Montella faces a significant selection headache with several key players ruled out through injury. The loss of Italy-based stars Hakan Çalhanoğlu and Kenan Yıldız severely impacts the team's creative options, while midfielder Orkun Kökçü is also highly doubtful due to a lingering toe injury.

In response to these absences, Montella is expected to shift Real Madrid prodigy Arda Güler into a central playmaker role to dictate the tempo of the attack.

Defensively, the experienced Merih Demiral will captain the side alongside Abdülkerim Bardakcı. The Crescent-Stars will rely heavily on the pace of Ferdi Kadıoğlu and Kerem Aktürkoğlu to stretch the Italian defence in this crucial UEFA Nations League fixture.

Italy manager Roberto Mancini has chosen a heavily rotated squad for this fixture, leaving ten players behind at the Coverciano training base to undergo specialised physical training.

Notable omissions from the travelling party include midfield engine Nicolò Barella and defender Gianluca Mancini .

The Azzurri are also hampered by injuries to key personnel, with Federico Dimarco , Bryan Cristante , and Manuel Locatelli all ruled out.

On a positive note, defensive rock Alessandro Bastoni returns to the starting lineup after serving a suspension. In attack, competition is fierce as Moise Kean and Gianluca Scamacca battle to lead the front line, supported by Daniel Maldini .

Mancini is also giving opportunities to rising talent, with Michael Kayode and midfielder Issa Doumbia pushing for significant minutes as Italy looks to test its squad depth while maintaining tactical flexibility.

Türkiye enters this clash in mixed form, adjusting to life in Europe's top tier after consecutive Nations League promotions. Their most recent outing ended in a narrow 1-0 defeat against France, where goalkeeper Uğurcan Çakır received a costly red card. Previously, their 2026 World Cup campaign yielded volatile results, including a 3-2 victory over the United States but also frustrating group-stage losses to Paraguay (0-1) and Australia (0-2).

Italy is struggling for consistency under returning manager Roberto Mancini. The Azzurri kicked off their Nations League campaign with a disappointing 2-0 loss to Belgium in Rome. Prior to that, Italy enjoyed back-to-back 1-0 friendly wins over Greece and Luxembourg in June. However, their competitive form remains fragile, highlighted by a painful penalty shootout exit to Bosnia and Herzegovina in the World Cup qualification finals back in March.

articles.title: A familiar road awaits Manchester City on the pitch when domestic football returns
articles.summary: With domestic football on pause for the extended international break, Manchester City has been the talk of the game after being found guilty of the majority...
articles.body:
With domestic football on pause for the extended international break, Manchester City has been the talk of the game after being found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges of breaching the Premier League's financial rules. David Ornstein broke the news for The Athletic that City had been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them. As of yet, there has been no official confirmation of this by the Premier League.

For now, matters on the pitch feel a mile away. Up next in the Premier League, Manchester City take on Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, the 11th of October. They will be facing a familiar situation. It is one that galvanised Pep Guardiola's side in previous seasons, famously in 2023. Whether or not it has the same effect in his new-look City side remains to be seen.

Pep Guardiola's Manchester City side put the outside noise aside famously in 2023.

The Premier League first charged Manchester City with 115 breaches of their financial fair play regulations back in February 2023. At the time, Pep Guardiola's side remained in the hunt for the treble. Ultimately, City would go on to famously claim the treble that season. There is no doubt that Pep Guardiola used the situation surrounding his side to galvanise his side. Pep Guardiola's side famously put the outside noise aside to create history. However, that City side was a far more experienced unit than this City outfit.

Manchester City's treble winning side that put the outside noise aside was full of leaders and experienced players. Kevin De Bruyne , Bernardo Silva , Ruben Dias , John Stones , Nathan Ake, Rodri , and Kyle Walker were all experienced leaders to lead City on the pitch through 2023. Pep Guardiola was also Manchester City's manager. Yes, Erling Haaland and Phil Foden were part of City's treble-winning side. Enzo Maresca was also Pep Guardiola's assistant. However, Haaland, Foden, and Maresca weren't as prominent figures at City as they are now.

Pep Guardiola turned the vitriol aimed at Manchester City back in 2023 into fuel for his team's fire. It is now up to a new City side to follow in their footsteps after David Ornstein's report landed last Friday.

Can Enzo Maresca and his City team put the outside noise aside?

Now, with the wolves at Manchester City's door, it falls on a new batch of City players and the manager and staff to galvanise their team. The City players, manager and staff can only focus on their job from here. That job is on the pitch and nowhere else. Courtroom battles are not their place or their area of expertise. The City players and fans will become targets for their opponents and opposing fans. That is the unfortunate by-product of the 115 saga. However, it could be a moment that fires up Enzo Maresca's side.

It will be fascinating to see how Enzo Maresca handles the entire situation. He will be front and centre of it all as Manchester City's manager. There is little doubt that he will be bombarded with questions about the entire affair. Pep Guardiola was defiant in his defence of his club. It would be expected that Maresca will likely follow suit in a public forum.

Also, how Enzo Maresca uses the situation to inspire his players will be of great interest. Maresca has players who have been here before in Erling Haaland, Phil Foden and Ruben Dias. Haaland and Dias are now leaders at Manchester City. They will be expected to rise above the outside noise, alongside City's other leaders, and lift their teammates. Manchester City's leader cannot control the uncontrollable. All they can do is attempt to continue to build upon their impressive start to the 2026-27 season. That is their remit for what lies in wait for Enzo Maresca's side when club football returns.

Manchester City have been down this road before. Pep Guardiola led his team defiantly and used the outside noise to fuel Manchester City's run to a historic treble. This time, the noise has gotten louder around City. Instead, it falls on a new manager and a new set of City players to put that noise aside and focus on what they can control.

A fierce reception likely awaits Enzo Maresca's side at Anfield on October 11. These players are made of the right stuff to handle it and rise above it. Their predecessors did and the challenge for this City side if to follow in their footsteps wherever that takes them.

articles.standfirst: El inicio de curso de la Real ha sido con muchas rotaciones, pero el defensa de Badalona es el único futbolista titular en los ocho partidos y con más de 600 minutos disputados
articles.summary: El inicio de curso de la Real ha sido con muchas rotaciones, pero el defensa de Badalona es el único futbolista titular en los ocho partidos y con más de 600 minutos disputados
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo ha utilizado a hasta 24 futbolistas en los ocho partidos que la Real Sociedad ha disputado en lo que llevamos de temporada 2026-27, al haber realizado habituales rotaciones por la cercanía de esos encuentros y la necesidad de dosificar esfuerzos. En un fútbol actual en el que hay un excel para controlar todo, Sergio Gómez parece estar por encima de ello, ya que es el único que ha hecho pleno de titularidades y se aproxima a los 700 minutos de juego, con clara ventaja sobre el resto. Sergio Gómez arrancó esta campaña como titular, porque la pasada ya se ganó claramente esa condición en el puesto de lateral izquierdo, tanto con Sergio Francisco, primero, como con Pellegrino Matarazzo, después, tras haber sido más comodín en la primera que estuvo en San Sebastián, a las órdenes de Imanol Alguacil. El caso es que el 17 de la plantilla txuriurdin ha salido en las fotos de los ocho equipos iniciales que ha sacado el técnico de Nueva Jersey en las siete jornadas de LaLiga y la de Europa League que se llevan, siendo el único del vestuario que puede decir eso. Sin duda, es un gran mérito, porque han sido hasta 24 los futbolistas utilizados en estos ocho primeros encuentros del curso, 20 de ellos siendo de la partida en alguno de ellos, al haber habido rotaciones en todas las posiciones, portería incluida, pero no en la del lateral zurdo. Por ello, ha sumado 681 de los 720 minutos disputados, no haciendo pleno por ser sustituido a falta de 18 y de 21 minutos ante Betis y Valencia, convirtiéndose por cierto en Centenario con la txuriurdin en Mestalla. Esos datos indican que Sergio Gómez no parece que esté tan condicionado al excel que controla todo en este inicio de curso. De hecho, esos 681 minutos le convierten en el futbolista más utilizado y con diferencia, ya que el siguiente es Jon Mikel Aramburu, con 597, a casi un partido por tanto de distancia. Tras no rotar antes del parón, habrá que ver si lo hace en los cinco partidos en sólo 15 días que habrá después o sigue al margen del contador de Matarazzo.

articles.title: Nations League: Northern Ireland players relish Windsor Park return against Hungary
articles.summary: Northern Ireland's hosting of Hungary in the Uefa Nations League will be their first game in Belfast for 315 days.
articles.body:
For the first time in 315 days, Northern Ireland are back in Belfast.

Michael O'Neill's side welcome Hungary to Windsor Park for a Nations League Group B2 contest on Monday night, just 51 days shy of a year since a Jamie Donley penalty saw the side to a 1-0 win over Luxembourg in their previous home fixture.

In the interim, they have played five times on their travels, a run that began with World Cup play-off defeat by Italy in Bergamo in March and concluded with victory over Georgia on Friday night.

If that win in Tbilisi represented a something of a breakthrough in terms of away performances - they had won just two of their previous 12 competitive away games - form back at Windsor has been strong despite the sporadic fixtures.

Since losing to Slovenia in October 2023, only Germany have left Belfast with a win and that a 1-0 triumph on a night the hosts missed numerous good chances.

A run of seven wins in nine home games is in stark contrast to what went before when, in the preceding nine at Windsor Park, Northern Ireland had beaten only San Marino and Kosovo, the latter courtesy of a 94th-minute winner.

O'Neill said he does not put much stock in such runs of form given the changing squads in international football, but acknowledged his team are in "a really good phase" at Windsor Park.

"This is a new team, so they're not saddled by the performance of previous teams," he said.

"They love playing here at the stadium. You know there was a period where the team of 2016 [who qualified for the European Championships of that year] didn't enjoy playing at home.

"Then suddenly they started to win games and they loved playing at home. Teams go through phases and at this moment in time this team is in a really good phase in terms of the home form."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One NI, BBC Three, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Ulster, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary available online.

"I'm buzzing for it," said midfielder Patrick Kelly who has picked up four of his five caps on the road.

"Obviously, I made my debut there last year in November time and I haven't played there since, it's all been away games.

"We haven't been there in a while and I'm really looking forward to it."

For goalkeeper Pierce Charles, who saved a penalty from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia against Georgia, the wait to play again at Windsor has been even longer.

"Personally, I've not played there in over a year now and I can't wait to feel the place rocking. I just can't wait to see the fans and hear how loud it's going to be," said the 22-year-old whose last game in Belfast was June 2025 thanks to injury.

"I think we thrive off it. It just makes us excited, playing in front of a positive crowd, especially when we're doing well.

"They love to get behind us, which we all love, so it just drives us on to do better."

Charles brothers 'brilliant' in NI's landmark win

O'Neill left 'baffled' by refereeing in late win

Monday night is, however, not an average home fixture.

Northern Ireland take to the field around 73 hours after the final whistle in Georgia with the game in Tbilisi having required an almost 5,000-mile trip. Indeed, O'Neill noted that Monday night's hosts will have travelled further to get to Belfast than the visitors given that Hungary played Ukraine in Budapest on Friday.

To mitigate the impact of the travel, Northern Ireland players were kept on UK-time throughout the trip despite the three-hour time difference and flew through the night to make it back to Belfast on Saturday morning.

"The preparation between games is pretty much the same. The difficulty with this game was obviously we had quite a distance to travel - we've travelled further than the away team in this situation," said O'Neill.

"But that's the draw and that's the nature of how the fixtures came out but this is a good group. I think they'll be ready to play."

articles.title: Man City charges: Case involving alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules could drag on for years
articles.summary: Sky Sports News understands that the process around Manchester City case is moving to the appeal stage, after reports claimed that most of the charges against the club for breaking Financial Fair Play rules were found to have been proven
articles.body:
According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands the process is moving to the appeal stage.

In 2014, City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play (FFP) rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m (£25.7m) for breaking the rules again.

The ban was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, where City were cleared of disguising owner funding as sponsorship income.

That victory may give City fans hope they can win again when their Premier League appeal is heard by a new three-person panel.

If the appeal goes against them they will not be able to go to CAS, but there is the strong possibility that City's owners would turn to the High Court to clear their name.

In 2014, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said he would spend £30m on the best 50 lawyers in the world and sue UEFA for the next 10 years rather than lose the FFP case.

In his open letter to City fans on Saturday, he sounded just as determined as he was 12 years ago: "The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began".

Al Mubarak means what he says and there is so much at stake that City will do whatever it takes to clear their name.

In the meantime, the most high-profile sports lawyers are keeping their thoughts to themselves until the full judgment is released. Friday's leak, which led to reports that City had lost on 114 of the 115 charges , may well end up being used as evidence in City's legal fight to prove that, in their opinion, the whole process has not been fair and impartial.

At the heart of all the legal challenges City have faced is the question of how they became so big and successful so quickly. City's owners have been accused of putting too much money into the club and disguising it as sponsorship income. City have always insisted they have irrefutable evidence to prove they did not break the rules.

City will face serious sanctions if they fail to clear their name and the case will continue to cast a shadow over Enzo Maresca and his players until it is finally resolved.

City's reputation, and that of their owners, depends on this and the final judgement will also have implications for relations between Abu Dhabi and the United Kingdom. The two countries have close ties and common trade and diplomatic interests, but the strength of that relationship will be tested if City are found definitively to have broken the rules.

City's legal dispute with the Premier League would never have existed if it had not been for documents obtained illegally by convicted Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto. From City's perspective, these leaked internal documents are "out-of-context materials purportedly hacked or stolen" which have been used in an "organised and clear attempt to damage the club's reputation".

articles.title: You are the new Scotland boss - what would you do?
articles.summary: Put yourself in the shoes of the new Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli as he picks his first home XI to face Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli takes charge of his first game at Hampden on Tuesday against Switzerland, live on the BBC, after an encouraging draw in his opening game away to Slovenia.

The Belgian chose eight uncapped players in his first squad with two of them - Robbie Ure and Stephen Welsh - making the starting XI in Ljubljana.

Ben Gannon-Doak and Kieron Bowie were the only substitutes used as Scotland dominated the second half but could not find a way to break the deadlock.

The Swiss represent a big step up in opposition, so will Pocognoli be tempted to tweak his team selection in Glasgow?

Scotland used three centre-backs on Saturday as Jack Hendry and Welsh flanked Scott McKenna.

Andy Robertson and Aaron Hickey were used as wing-backs, tasked with whipping crosses in for the attacking duo of Oli McBurnie and Ure.

There were some worrying signs in the opening 45 minutes in Slovenia as the hosts routinely stole in behind Scotland's high line.

However, it is unlikely the new boss will move away from his defensive strategy so early in his reign.

"We had a lot of good movement through the side, through the lines and we should have scored to be honest," he said after the goalless game.

"But the counter-press was good, the high [line] of the defence was good, just because the position of the players was better [in the second half].

"Clean sheet, that's also positive, but we want to win."

Uncapped pair Luis Binks and Luke Graham are the other centre-halves in the squad, so there's a good chance we see the same trio starting.

At the weekend, Gannon-Doak was introduced with just over 10 minutes and added menace to Scotland's attack.

Although he replaced Hickey, the Bournemouth winger is not an obvious fit at wing-back.

Might Pocognoli be tempted to use his searing pace up top rather than go with two strikers?

With four Nations League matches across 11 days in this window, utilising the squad will be key.

Hearts winger Josh McPake could also add a different dimension to the front line, after a bright start to the season for Hearts.

John McGinn started as a number 10 in Slovenia and was rather subdued but his experience, running power and goal threat make him such a key player for Scotland.

Billy Gilmour was the stand-out performer on Pocognoli's debut and really took the game by the scruff of the neck in the second half.

He was part of a double pivot with Serie A pal Lewis Ferguson but took up a more advanced role after the break, popping up regularly around the edge of the penalty box.

If there is to be a midfield change, Ryan Christie offers relentless energy and can fit in just about anywhere. Under Steve Clarke he did not get many chances in the middle of the park where he has done so well for Bournemouth.

Kieron Bowie, Robbie Ure and Oli McBurnie are the striker options, and all three are in good form and confident.

Ure and McBurnie are yet to score for their clubs this term, but both showed, in flashes, why they were given the starting nods by Pocognoli.

McBurnie, who dropped a little deeper after half-time, is the oldest and comfortably the most experienced of the trio but has yet to score after racking up 17 caps.

He should have done better with a chance against the imposing Jan Oblak, who pinched the ball off his feet.

Ure was described as "elegant" and showing "effortless" movement by pundit Pat Nevin during the game. He contested 18 duels in his time on the park - the most of any Scotland player.

He was determined to make an impact on his debut and went close to scoring with a strike that crashed off the post on the stroke of half time.

Off the bench with roughly 20 minutes to go, Bowie was a smart addition too, although the Sassuolo forward should have put Scotland ahead when he pulled an effort wide of the post.

The big question for the boss is do two of the three start against the Swiss, who were comfortable 3-0 winners in North Macedonia, or is there a need for speed or an extra man in midfield?

articles.title: Osvaldo está "bien y lúcido" tras su intervención en el pulmón
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista de 40 años permanece internado en Llavallol tras ser intervenido por un derrame pleural
articles.summary: El exfutbolista de 40 años permanece internado en Llavallol tras ser intervenido por un derrame pleural
articles.body: El exfutbolista y músico Daniel Osvaldo permanece internado en la Unidad de Terapia Intensiva del Hospital Municipal de Llavallol tras haber ingresado el pasado jueves por la noche con un severo cuadro infeccioso en la zona pulmonar. Según confirmaron sus allegados y familiares, el exdelantero de 40 años se encuentra "lúcido", sin ningún tipo de sedación y "estable". No obstante, los profesionales médicos decidieron mantenerlo en cuidados intensivos de manera preventiva hasta obtener precisiones sobre su evolución. El problema de salud comenzó días atrás, cuando el exjugador de Boca y la selección italiana sintió un fuerte malestar que inicialmente confundió con un resfrío común. Al acudir al centro médico, los profesionales le detectaron un derrame pleural derecho con presencia de líquido y pus, por lo que debió ser intervenido quirúrgicamente de urgencia para drenar la zona afectada. Durante la operación se tomaron muestras biológicas que fueron enviadas a laboratorio para realizar la correspondiente biopsia. Por el momento, los médicos no han podido determinar qué microorganismo provocó la infección, por lo que el diagnóstico definitivo continúa en suspenso a la espera de los resultados analíticos. Desde el entorno familiar llevaron tranquilidad al señalar que el cuadro fue detectado a tiempo y que, en función de cómo respondan los análisis de la biopsia, los especialistas evaluarán en los próximos días si está en condiciones de ser trasladado a una sala de internación general.

articles.title: Is supporting Everton a life of misery - or celebration?
articles.summary: Is supporting Everton a life of misery, or are there still reasons to celebrate? Chief football writer Phil McNulty seeks the answer.
articles.body:
Everton 's unbeaten start to the Premier League season and progress in the Carabao Cup has prompted a minor outbreak of something rarely felt among their fanbase in recent times - optimism.

Guarded optimism, understandably, but the mood has shifted somewhat since the fury that followed a badly botched transfer window, typified by a shambolic final day that left manager David Moyes with only 18 senior outfield players.

A move for AS Monaco striker Falorin Balogun fell through when he walked away from the deal after problems with the medical, while Iliman Ndiaye, arguably Everton 's best player, was sold to Manchester City for £65m.

It is against this backdrop that Moyes seeks to end Everton 's 31-year search for success that has saddled them with an unwanted record.

Since the turn of the century, Everton are the only club in English football's current top four tiers who have not won a trophy - their last being the 1995 FA Cup triumph against Manchester United at the old Wembley - or been promoted.

Of course, to the enjoy the rush of promotion, Everton would first have to suffer the pain of relegation.

It nearly happened this millennium as Everton - last relegated in 1951 - stayed up by beating Bournemouth on the final day of the 2022-23 season. They had only guaranteed safety in the previous campaign by coming from two goals down to beat Crystal Palace in their penultimate game on a night of thunderous sporting theatre at Goodison Park.

So is supporting Everton a life of unrelenting sporting misery? Or is there still joy and celebration to be had following of one the grand old English football institutions?

Former player Leon Osman, who made 433 appearances for Everton between 2003 and 2016, scoring 58 goals, says: "Yes, there have been disappointments and those years without trophies, but let me tell you this - I wouldn't swap being an Evertonian for anything in the world."

And prominent Everton fan Dr. David France, who calculates he has travelled two million miles - the equivalent of going to the moon and back four times - to watch his beloved club from his home in the United States, told BBC Sport: "I can explain what I celebrate, even if we haven't had tangible success for so long. I celebrate being an Evertonian."

Others who also celebrate supporting Everton include Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Canada counterpart Mark Carney, who recently both attended the 1-0 EFL Cup win against Wolverhampton Wanderers at Hill Dickinson Stadium that set up a last-16 home tie with Newcastle United .

Moyes demands more from Everton - but don't mention Europe

The statistics that pile pain on Everton and their fans reflect those occasional highs and more regular lows - but always accompanied by fiercely passionate, loyal support and sold-out games, at Goodison Park and the magnificent new Hill Dickinson Stadium.

And Everton remain one of only six Premier League originals, along with Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur , who have never dropped out of the top tier.

Elsewhere, Everton 's tale of the tape is not so flattering.

Since 2000, they have lost two FA Cup semi-finals, winning a third against Manchester United on penalties in 2009, only to lose to Chelsea in the final.

Everton have been knocked out eight times at the first time of asking in the third round.

In the EFL Cup, they have only reached the semi-finals twice, in 2008 and 2016, losing both.

In the league since 2000, Everton have failed to win at Chelsea in 27 attempts, won only twice at Manchester United , once at Arsenal and Liverpool and five times at Manchester City . Everton did win an FA Cup fourth-round replay at Stamford Bridge in 2011.

In the 53 Merseyside derbies in the Premier League in this time, Everton have won only five and lost 28.

Their ledger is balanced by a dramatic FA Cup fourth-round replay win against Liverpool in 2009, secured with Dan Gosling's last-minute goal in extra-time, as well as a crucial 1-0 derby win that was part of their finest season in this fallow period.

In 2004-05, Everton manager David Moyes performed what then Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger described as "a miracle" when, after selling Wayne Rooney to Manchester United , he guided them to fourth place and into the Champions League.

It was a campaign that contained another of Everton 's celebratory moments, when Duncan Ferguson tormented Sir Alex Ferguson's Manchester United , scoring the winner with a trademark header from Mikel Arteta's free-kick on another memorable Goodison night.

Sadly, Everton 's journey into the Champions League qualifying round ended in heartbreak and controversy when, after losing the first leg 2-1 at home to eventual semi-finalists Villarreal, referee Pierluigi Collina mysteriously ruled out a late Ferguson header that would have sent the tie into extra-time.

They eventually went out 4-2 on aggregate following a decision that still rankles today.

Osman is well qualified to answer, having enjoyed a distinguished first-team career at Everton stretching between 2003 and 2016.

He told BBC Sport: "We've had some disappointments in those times, certainly in terms of not winning anything, but we've had some good days along the way, good moments.

"We've reached semi-finals, an FA Cup final, some great celebrations. We had some great trips in Europe - I think about us winning in Nuremberg in the Uefa Cup with thousands of our fans there to enjoy it.

"I certainly don't feel it's been 26 years of misery. I would argue very strongly against that. When we qualified for the Champions League in 2005, that was an incredible achievement, given the clubs we were up against. We did something very special in that season."

Osman added: "I am more than upset than any Evertonian in the world that we haven't won anything in the last 20-30 years, certainly in the period I played when I could affect it, but there has never been a single moment when I would swap being an Evertonian for anyone else.

"It's better to be an Evertonian than to support any other club, and you mark my words, if and when we do get silverware, just you watch those celebrations. They will be something else."

The fan's verdict comes from Dr. France, whose devotion to Everton can be measured in those two million miles.

This is the result of countless transatlantic trips the 78-year-old has made from Arizona in the United States, the country which has been his base since 1977.

Dr. France is no ordinary Everton fan, attending his first game on 4 September 1957 when Everton drew 3-3 with Manchester United 's Busby Babes.

He established the Everton Former Players' Foundation in 1999, and is the club's premier archivist, with more than 20,000 items of memorabilia, which he transferred into public ownership via The Everton Collection Charitable Trust and is now maintained at the Liverpool Record Office.

"I think we missed the boat after the Premier League ship sailed. We are no longer the best of the rest," Dr. France acknowledges.

"For about a 10-year period under David Moyes we averaged about sixth or seventh and we had the odd hard-luck story, and more recently for a three-year period we could almost be described as a laughing stock. Hopefully that's no longer the case.

"We aren't with the Aston Villas and the Newcastles, who are challenging for the best of the rest, but we live in hope."

And how much has his devotion to Everton cost him?

"A robust seven-figure Littlewoods Pools jackpot," he says in a nod to the company formed by Everton 's patriarch of the 1960s and 1970s Sir John Moores, whose vast fortune earned the club the nickname 'The Mersey Millionaires'.

"If I'm picking one recent celebration at a game," says Dr. France, "it would be our 2-0 win over Liverpool at Goodison in April 2024 - our first win in 30 derbies, excluding the 2-0 win behind closed doors at Anfield [during the Covid-19 pandemic].

"I was sitting in the second row of the directors' box and three rows behind me was a certain Andy Burnham, fists clenched and punching the Merseyside air.

"I'm very lucky to be part of something very special supporting Everton . It is a special community. You don't become an Evertonian to be a glory hunter do you?

"We have loyalty inbred into us. We don't just support the club, Evertonians support one another. We are a family. When I go to watch Everton , I feel like I'm among friends."

And he hopes he and those fellow Everton fans will have something to celebrate soon.

articles.title: Ireland players wear black armbands and refrain from handshakes in Israel soccer game
articles.summary: There were no handshakes between Ireland and Israel players before their contentious Nations League match on Sunday, with the Irish team wearing black armbands for its 3-0 victory.
articles.body: DEBRECEN, Hungary — There were no handshakes between Ireland and Israel players before their contentious Nations League match on Sunday, with the Irish team wearing black armbands for its 3-0 victory. The game faced bitter opposition in Ireland over Israel’s actions in Gaza with the players coming under huge pressure to boycott two matches against Israel. Reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazuno decided Saturday to leave the squad for both games because of what he said was his “personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong.” The Irish players looked down at the grass with their heads bowed and hands behind their backs during the playing of the Israeli national anthem, and Irish captain Dara O’Shea approached the center of the field for the pre-match talk with his hands still firmly clasped behind his back. O’Shea shook hands with the referee and his assistants but there was no attempt to shake the hand of Israel captain Manor Solomon. There was a small group of Israeli fans in the otherwise almost-empty stadium in Debrecen, Hungary, but an even smaller group of around 10 people without colors were celebrating when Troy Parrott broke the deadlock in the 13th minute. There weren’t supposed to be any Irish fans present. Some Ireland supporters who managed to get tickets through the Israeli soccer federation told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that those had been canceled Saturday night. Adam Idah made it 2-0 three minutes after Parrott’s opener and Jack Moylan got the third goal in the 25th. Ireland needed goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher at his best to deny Israel after the break, and tempers became frayed around the hour mark after a clash between Idah and Raz Shlomo. Both players were booked by German referee Harm Osmers. Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was suspended for the game after his sending off following his goal-celebration in Thursday’s 3-1 loss to Austria. Ireland and Israel meet again on Oct. 4 in Ireland’s “home” game in Backa Topola, Serbia.

articles.title: Belgium vs France – Nations League: Team line-ups, head-to-head, Mbappe
articles.summary: Two-time world champions France travel to Belgium for Monday’s Nations League clash without captain Kylian Mbappe.
articles.body:
Who : Belgium vs France What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A1 match Where : King Baudouin Stadium, Brussels, Belgium When : Monday, September 28, at 8:45pm (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT

Captain Kylian Mbappe did his part by giving France the winning start they aimed for in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, but a knee injury will keep him out of action when the two-time world champions face Belgium on Monday.

Mbappe’s early second-half strike in France’s 1-0 win over Turkiye in the opening match was marred by his injury, and the country’s leading scorer will be out of action for two weeks.

The visitors have no shortage of talent and goal-scoring skills, though, as the talented trio of Michael Olise, Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue will take responsibility in front of goal on match day two of the competition.

Their neighbours, Belgium, bolstered by the experienced Kevin De Bruyne, also made a winning start by beating Italy 2-0 in Rome and will no doubt pose a tough challenge for the French visitors.

Interestingly, Monday’s contest will see new coaches in the hot seat, with former Dutch international Mark van Bommel taking over the reins at Belgium and the legendary Zinedine Zidane , a former France midfielder, returning to the coaching job.

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against top-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure, which features promotion and relegation.

They last met in a Nations League group encounter in October 2024, with Randal Kolo Muani’s double giving France a 2-1 win over Belgium.

De Bruyne and Diego Moreira (Belgium) : Veteran De Bruyne, known for pulling the strings in midfield, grabbed the limelight in the last game with his assist and man-of-the-match performance. Fans should also watch out for Diego Moreira on the left wing following his three goals in as many league games for AC Milan this term.

Olise and Rayan Cherki (France) : Winger Olise was the man of the match last time out and has made a flying start at Bayern Munich this season with eight goals and four assists in seven matches across all competitions. Furthermore, Rayan Cherki has also found the net for his club, Manchester City, bagging four goals and two assists.

Zinedine Zidane (France) : “There will be changes. How many? You’ll see. We knew we’d have four matches in such a short time, so we’re going to rotate the squad a little. The most important thing is to get to know each other.”

Mark van Bommel (Belgium) : “It is special to coach against someone like that. He [Zidane] was an exceptional footballer, and I played against him once, with Barcelona against Real Madrid. If a dribbling move is named after you, then you must have done pretty well. He is a good coach too; that’s clear.”

They have two injuries in the squad – winger Leandro Trossard has a heel injury and goalkeeper Mike Penders has a muscle issue.

Probable Belgium XI : Senne Lammens; Timothy Castagne, Nathan Ngoy, Brandon Mechele, Maxim De Cuyper; Nicolas Raskin; Dodi Lukebakio, Kevin De Bruyne, Youri Tielemans, Diego Moreira; Charles De Ketelaere

Mbappe is the highest-profile international missing from the squad for Monday’s game, with the Real Madrid striker sidelined with a knee injury until mid-October. Central midfielder Warren Zaire-Emery is also out with a thigh injury, while defensive midfielder Matteo Guendouzi is suspended.

articles.title: Aaron Ramsdale: What has gone wrong for ex-Arsenal goalkeeper at Southampton?
articles.summary: From challenging for the Premier League with Arsenal and playing for England, Aaron Ramsdale is now Southampton's fourth-choice goalkeeper.
articles.body:
In April 2023, Aaron Ramsdale was within touching distance of winning the Premier League with Arsenal.

But the goalkeeper made a costly error for the Gunners to give away the opening goal in a 3-3 draw with Southampton at Emirates Stadium which contributed to the demise of Arsenal's 2022-23 title bid.

If Arsenal had won that game, the title would have been in their hands. Instead, the draw handed the initiative to Manchester City, who took full advantage.

It was a mistake which perhaps also signalled the beginning of the end for Ramsdale under Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Four months later, the north London club brought in David Raya from Brentford and the Spaniard quickly claimed the number one spot.

And in a somewhat unfortunate poetic twist, it is the Saints where Ramsdale finds himself completely out of favour three years on as the fourth-choice goalkeeper at a Championship club.

From an England international on the cusp of greatness, Ramsdale is now in the almost unthinkable situation of being without senior football this season in the prime of his career at the age of 28.

So why has Ramsdale had such a fall from grace and where have things gone wrong?

Questions were raised among the Arsenal fanbase when the club paid £24m to sign Ramsdale from Sheffield United in August 2021 after the Blades had been relegated from the top flight.

But he quickly won supporters over by producing a string of excellent saves in his debut season, perhaps most notably against Leicester City when he denied a James Maddison free-kick at full stretch - a save which Peter Schmeichel described at the time as "the best I've seen for years".

After ousting Bernd Leno, his efforts helped Arsenal finish fifth in 2021-22, improving on an eighth-placed finish the previous year.

The following season, Ramsdale was a vital cog in Arsenal's spine as they launched a surprise title challenge, only to be outdone by an imperious Manchester City side.

Despite his blunder in the draw with Southampton - which was one of several results that dented Arsenal's title hopes - Ramsdale made the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) team of the year and was also named goalkeeper of the year at the London Football Awards.

But Ramsdale quickly fell behind Raya in the pecking order in 2023-24 and lost his starting berth after just four league games.

And in one of the only two other Premier League matches he did play that season against Raya's then parent club Brentford, Ramsdale made another mistake to allow Yoane Wissa to put the Bees ahead.

Arsenal recovered to win that game 2-1 in March 2024. But Ramsdale never played for the club again.

He was sold to Southampton for £25m in August 2024 after returning from Euro 2024 with England, having been an unused sub throughout the competition in Germany.

A fourth relegation and failed Newcastle loan

At the time of Ramsdale's signing, he looked to be the perfect goalkeeper and a coup for Southampton.

Russell Martin's side had just won promotion and were hoping to implement a style of play in the Premier League that had brought them such success the previous season.

Ramsdale ticked all the boxes as a goalkeeper who had ability with his feet to complement Martin's preference to build up from the back.

His previous spells at Sheffield United and Bournemouth also justified his addition as someone whose stock had continued to rise despite being involved in relegations.

Ultimately, though, the move to Southampton did not work out as planned.

He made 30 league appearances for a Saints side which finished bottom of the Premier League with just 12 points - the second-lowest ever points tally in the competition - and conceded more goals (66) than any other goalkeeper in 2024-25.

That is not to say Ramsdale was to blame in a Southampton side which performed poorly across the board, with some fans at the time in fact praising him for keeping the score down in games.

It would, however, be the fourth relegation Ramsdale had suffered, having already done so with Chesterfield, while on loan in 2017-18, the Cherries in 2019-20 - although he was named player of the year for Bournemouth that season - and then the Blades.

After signing from Sheffield United in 2017, Ramsdale was an understudy to experienced goalkeeper Asmir Begovic at the Vitality Stadium for two years before his breakthrough.

"First of all, Aaron's a fantastic goalkeeper," Begovic told BBC Sport.

"We first worked together about nine years ago and since then he's been on an incredible ride where he's performed at the highest level.

"I remember my remit when I came into Bournemouth was to mentor and set a tone for some of the younger goalkeepers, one of which was Aaron Ramsdale.

"There's many different factors that go into it but I think it's been unfortunate that maybe a few things haven't aligned for him [at Southampton]."

Southampton's relegation prompted Ramsdale to seek top flight football once more and he moved to Newcastle United on loan for the 2025-26 campaign.

But again, what was supposed to be a move to help re-establish his career at the highest level did not come to pass.

Ramsdale kept just two clean sheets in 23 appearances in all competitions for the Magpies, featuring only 12 times in the Premier League - and neither he nor Nick Pope could make the number one spot permanently their own.

He also had the unfortunate experience of letting in seven goals in one game in a 7-2 defeat by Barcelona in the Champions League last-16 - the most he has ever conceded in a single game.

Follow Southampton content on BBC Sounds

Pre-match, post-match and topical Saints content

'Very difficult and frustrating' - what next for Ramsdale?

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has seemingly made it clear Ramsdale is not part of his plans this season, with Daniel Peretz his number one, George Long the second choice and Jamie Jones returning to the club as mainly a training goalkeeper.

"The reality is that Rambo's story with the football club started before myself," Eckert told BBC Radio Solent .

"We've had honest conversations from the first day of pre-season until the very last day of the transfer window.

"The expectations for him are clear to support the team in the best way and he's been very professional in doing that so far."

Despite his exclusion so far this season, Ramsdale is said to have a good relationship with Eckert, the coaching staff and the other goalkeepers - and has an affection for the club.

Ramsdale also believes there is a route back into the first team for him at St Mary's and is willing to fight for his place until at least January, when the winter transfer window opens.

He had offers on the table in the summer to go on loan to clubs in England, Spain and Italy but declined, with his current ambition to try to help Southampton win promotion back to the Premier League and play in the top flight.

As well as being a popular figure in the dressing room and well-liked by Saints supporters, Ramsdale also had personal factors to consider for what would have been a move to a fourth club in four years.

His wife recently gave birth to their second child and the family are settled in the area, with Ramsdale only wanting to change clubs if it was the right opportunity.

Begovic says his former team-mate will be finding his current lack of playing time "very difficult and frustrating".

"I had a few spells where I was frozen out at a club for a short time but I can't really relate to Aaron's situation," he added.

"I can imagine there will be some factors that are out of his hands. In the meantime he'll have to make sure that he trains well and stays fit and be ready if an opportunity comes up to play.

"He has to be ready for the long term and if the chance to move elsewhere comes up, he's ready.

"I'd love to see Aaron playing again and hopefully it happens in January but I'm fully aware that it won't be a straightforward situation."

articles.title: El rajadón de Álvaro Vadillo contra Óscar García: "Era horrorosamente malo"
articles.standfirst: El extremo andaluz ha hablado de su breve etapa en el Celta
articles.summary: El extremo andaluz ha hablado de su breve etapa en el Celta
articles.body: Álvaro Vadillo ha vuelto a hablar, varios años después, de su corta experiencia en el Celta de Vigo. El exfutbolista apenas permaneció tres meses en el conjunto gallego y no llegó a disputar un solo partido oficial. Ahora, en una entrevista en el podcast Climbers, repasó aquella etapa y señaló directamente al entonces entrenador celeste, Óscar García. Vadillo llegó a Vigo en el verano de 2020 después de haber quedado libre tras su etapa en el Granada. Sin embargo, desde el comienzo de la pretemporada comprobó que su situación no iba a ser sencilla. Ante la falta de minutos, el jugador decidió hablar con el entonces director deportivo del Celta para intentar entender qué estaba ocurriendo. "¿Ustedes me habéis firmado con el sí del entrenador? Porque esto no tiene ni pies ni cabeza", recordó que le planteó a Felipe Miñambres. La situación no mejoró. Según su relato, disputados cinco encuentros de preparación, ni siquiera había tenido la oportunidad de entrar al campo: "Antes de que cerrara el mercado jugamos cinco partidos y no es que no jugara ni uno, es que ni calenté. Es que muchas veces es para reírte". El recuerdo de Vadillo sobre su entrenador de aquella época es especialmente duro. El exjugador no cuestionó únicamente las decisiones deportivas del técnico, sino también su trato personal con la plantilla. "Yo fui tonto y niñatillo. Óscar García era el entrenador de esa época y era horrorosamente malo. No te hablo a nivel deportivo, sino un tío que llega allí y no te da los buenos días... malo. Ni saludaba a nadie, serio. Todos los entrenamientos los hacía el segundo entrenador. Horroroso, y como persona peor porque ni te saluda", señaló. Vadillo terminó saliendo del Celta rumbo al Espanyol apenas tres meses después de su llegada a Vigo. El futbolista reconoció que, visto con perspectiva, debería haber esperado su oportunidad en lugar de precipitar su salida. "Yo debería haber dicho 'este tío va a durar poco aquí, me voy a callar y voy a seguir entrenando y estar en forma para cuando me llegue el momento', pero fui caprichoso y no quería estar ahí", concluyó, reflexionando sobre lo que fue su etapa en Vigo: "Tres meses es mi estancia en Vigo con cero partidos oficiales, esto no lo tiene nadie. El Celta hizo un negocio redondo, me coge libre, no paga el sueldo porque el Espanyol paga la ficha entera y luego saca 1,7 kilos".

articles.title: Jürgen Klopp y el peor arranque de un seleccionador en la historia de Alemania
articles.standfirst: Empate ante Países Bajos y derrota contra Grecia en sus dos primeros partidos
articles.summary: Empate ante Países Bajos y derrota contra Grecia en sus dos primeros partidos
articles.body: Aunque esto no es cómo acaba y sí cómo termina, el dato es demoledor: tras empatar con Paises Bajos (1-1) y perder con Grecia (0-1), Jürgen Klopp se ha convertido en el seleccionador con peor arranque en la historia de la Selección de Alemania. Sepp Herberger (1937) y Helmut Schön (1965) ya habían empezado sin victoria tras dos jornadas... pero al menos ellos habían empatado ambos partidos. "Ya sabía antes de venir aquí que el fútbol alemán no se encuentra actualmente en su mejor momento y que Jürgen Klopp no iba a llegar y resolver todos los problemas con un simple gesto de la mano. Si alguien no lo sabía, ahora ya lo sabe. Los avances nunca son lo suficientemente grandes. Las cosas nunca suceden lo suficientemente rápido. Pero, con el tiempo, en un futuro próximo, llegará un momento en el que cualquier rival tendrá dificultades para enfrentarse a nosotros", declaraba, en tercera persona, el ex entrenador del Liverpool. La situación de Alemania es delicada y no triunfar con la 'Mannschaft' no descalabra automáticamente una carrera como entrenador. Que se lo digan a Hansi Flick, que fue muy criticado, apenas estuvo 25 partidos como seleccionador y ahora ha construido un equipo tremendamente dominante en Barcelona. Pero es evidente que Alemania tiene muchos problemas. Una situación similar a la que vive Italia... aunque al menos los germanos sí han estado en las últimas tres Copas del Mundo. "Ya no somos un equipo de primera categoría. Ahora solo somos un equipo mediocre. Ya no contamos con jugadores que marquen la diferencia. Incluso Grecia tiene a Karetsas, Tzolis y Pavlidis; para mí, esos son jugadores que marcan la diferencia. Esperemos que Jürgen Klopp consiga formar un equipo capaz de practicar el fútbol de Klopp", analizaba Schweinsteiger en la TV alemana tras el descalabro de Alemania ante los helenos. "No hay motivo para que caiga en la depresión y diga: “Somos muy malos”. No lo somos. Pero tampoco somos tan buenos", analizaba Klopp en la versión 'smart' de aquella mítica frase de Manolo Preciado. "Si queréis criticar a alguien, criticadme a mí. Dejad que los nuevos jugadores se desarrollen. Los jugadores consolidados son jugadores de primer nivel en sus clubes y cuentan con mi apoyo. Criticadme a mí si queréis, pero no a los chicos. No hace falta destrozarlo todo por completo. Me sorprendió que algunas personas abuchearan. El futuro es tan prometedor como lo hagamos nosotros. Lo afrontaremos con todo lo que tenemos. Seguiremos por este camino", cerraba su análisis Jürgen. Tiene ahora dos partidos más para enderezar la situación: recibir a Serbia... y visitar Grecia.

articles.title: Boston-bound Delta flight makes emergency landing in Portugal due to smoke in cabin
articles.summary: A Delta flight from Barcelona to Boston made an emergency landing on Sunday afternoon in Porto, Portugal, the airline operator said.
articles.body: A Delta flight from Barcelona to Boston made an emergency landing on Sunday afternoon in Porto, Portugal, the airline operator said. Flight DL251 was diverted to Porto following a reported mechanical issue and landed there safely, the company said. Flight data from tracking service Flightradar24 suggested the plane left Barcelona at 3:15 p.m. (1315 GMT) and landed in Porto at 5:45 p.m. (1645 GMT). Eight passengers who had been onboard the Airbus A330 plane were treated on the tarmac at Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport in Porto while three others were taken to hospital for treatment, a spokesperson for Portugal’s emergency and civil protection authority told Reuters by phone. The forced landing was due to smoke in the cabin, the Portuguese spokesperson added.

articles.title: Axel Tapé, único granota con actividad internacional
articles.standfirst: El jugador galo, que no ha debutado con la camiseta granota, fue titular con su selección en la Liga Elite
articles.summary: El jugador galo, que no ha debutado con la camiseta granota, fue titular con su selección en la Liga Elite
articles.body: Aún no ha debutado con la camiseta granota pero Axel Tapé es el único jugador del Levante que ha tenido actividad en esta ventana internacional. El centrocampista francés fue titular en el choque que enfrentaba a la selección de Francia sub-20 y Alemania en la Liga Elite que se disputa en la ciudad de La Nucía. El galo fue protagonista en la derrota del combinado galo, por un gol a cero, ante los germanos gracias a un tanto en el tramo final del partido. Este próximo martes, el equipo del gallo volverá a los terrenos de juego a las 11:30 horas frente a Inglaterra y este sábado, 3 de octubre, ante Italia, a las 11:00 horas. Las otras dos ausencias del conjunto granota, por cuestiones de citaciones con sus selecciones, son Nacho Pérez y Ifeany Ndukwe. El lateral español, que ha estado concentrado en la sub19, se reincorporará mañana con el grupo en la Ciudad Deportiva de Buñol, tras terminar su estadía en Marbella. Por su parte, el jugador austriaco se enfrentará ante Dinamarca, el próximo 2 de octubre, y ante Gales, el próximo martes día 6, en la fase de clasificación para el campeonato de Europa de 2027. En esta segunda semana de parón por selecciones, el Levante repetirá la misma dinámica que los últimos siete días. El equipo volverá este martes a los entrenamientos y se ejercitarán hasta el próximo viernes.

articles.title: Los fichajes del Córdoba decepcionan por ahora
articles.standfirst: El mal arranque liguero del equipo se explica en parte por el discreto nivel o la caída en el rendimiento inicial de sus caras nuevas
articles.summary: El mal arranque liguero del equipo se explica en parte por el discreto nivel o la caída en el rendimiento inicial de sus caras nuevas
articles.body: El Córdoba volvió a decepcionar en Valladolid y cerrará el mes de septiembre con números pobres, sólo 6 puntos de 21 posibles. Es justo lo mismo que selló el curso pasado y luego reaccionó, por lo que siempre hay que mantener una cierta cautela. Y, aunque evidentemente de fondo hay un problema colectivo siempre, en parte el arranque se explica en parte por el discreto nivel o la caída en el rendimiento inicial de las caras nuevas, que, se supone, siempre vienen a dar un salto de calidad. Sin entrar ya en el hecho de que Nelson Monte ni haya debutado aún cuando se esperaba como un fichaje relevante en la defensa, que Ibai Sanz y Damián Cáceres prácticamente no cuenten (un partido jugaron solamente cada uno) y que El Jebari haya debutado ahora tras llegar lesionado en pretemporada del pubis, pocos de los refuerzos están llamando la atención. O, en algún caso, lo hacen pero para mal hasta ahora. Por ejemplo, la entrada de Guilherme Fernandes en la portería no ha mejorado en nada los números de Iker Álvarez. 7 tantos encajó el andorrano, ninguno de ellos puramente de un gran error personal, y el luso lleva 9 y con varios con evidente responsabilidad, como pasó en Valladolid. Otro caso importante es el de Juan Gutiérrez, otra vez muy vulnerable en Pucela y ahora mismo lejísimos de lo que se esperaba de él. Luego hay otros futbolistas cuyo rendimiento o bien la caída en el mismo ya han merecido que Iván Ania deje de contar con ellos. Es el caso de Tasende y Eder García, que pasaron al banquillo directamente para no tener ni un minuto en este último partido. Mientras, en el lateral derecho Egoitz y Budesca han ido alternando buenos momentos con errores sobre todo en la marca que les han hecho ir saliendo y entrando. En cuanto a Diarra, que arrancó a alto nivel, está muy apagado en los últimos encuentros. En Valladolid, el Córdoba jugó con Álex Martín, Rubén Alves, Albarrán, Isma Ruiz, Carracedo, Kevin Medina y Diego Percan, es decir, 7 jugadores de la temporada pasada. Varios de ellos tampoco estuvieron bien, por lo que se ve que no es algo exclusivo de los fichajes, aunque es una situación significativa. Las apuestas realizadas por la Comisión Deportiva están dejando muchas dudas en los encuentros iniciales de Liga.

articles.title: Éric García ya está en Barcelona: máxima precaución, aunque sólo sufre un edema en la rodilla
articles.standfirst: El defensa, que fue examinado hoy por el Barça, guardará reposo en los próximos días
articles.summary: El defensa
articles.body: Eric García ya está en casa. El central catalán no jugó el primer encuentro de la selección española, disputado el pasado sábado contra Inglaterra en Wembley, a causa de unas molestias en la rodilla izquierda. Iba a ser titular, pero fue desconvocado. Por precaución. Ya está en Barcelona. La dolencia no es importante, en estos momentos sólo tiene un edema, pero en el Barça irán con máxima cautela en su regreso al trabajo. Siguen una estricta política de cero riesgo con todos sus profesionales. Hoy fue examinado por los servicios médicos del Barça, aunque no se sometió a nuevas pruebas. El central catalán, de 25 años, notó unas molestias en su rodilla izquierda, durante el entrenamiento previo al cruce de la Nations League contra Inglaterra, y tras someterse a pruebas, la RFEF decidió desconvocarlo. No sufría ninguna lesión, pero la selección apostó por preservarlo. Iba a ser titular en el lateral derecho del combinado de Luis de la Fuente. El Barça aplaude y agradece la decisión de la Federación, que también entiende como lógica, y seguirá con el planteamiento de evitar cualquier riesgo o poner en peligro la rodilla de su futbolista. Irán con máxima cautela con su incorporación al trabajo y en la planificación de las rutinas de entrenamiento y el aumento de cargas. Nadie desea que lo que ahora es solo un edema, según pudo saber MARCA, se convierta en un problema más serio. Además, se trata de una articulación delicada, e irán con mucha precaución. El futbolista se pasó este lunes por la Ciudad Deportiva para ser examinado por los servicios médicos culés, que también descartaron una dolencia importante aunque no le sometieron a más pruebas y dieron por satisfactorias las realizadas por la Federación. El Barça regresa a los entrenamientos el lunes 5 de octubre y disputa el primer partido el sábado 10 a las 18:30 en el Spotify Camp Nou contra el Getafe. En función de su evolución, Eric estará a disposición o no de Flick. De momento, el profesional azulgrana, un hombre fundamental en el esquema del entrenador alemán (ha participado en seis encuentros de LaLiga, en todos fue titular en el lateral derecho), tendrá que guardar reposo unos días. Próximamente, una vez se haya reducido el edema, ya comenzará la recuperación. Pero se irá poco a poco.
