articles.title: Manchester City charges: Roberto Mancini says Premier League rule breaches 'not my concern'
articles.summary: Roberto Mancini says an alleged "double contract" during his time as Manchester City manager is "not my concern".
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini says an alleged "double contract" during his time as Manchester City manager is "not my concern" after the club were found guilty of breaking the majority of the financial rules they were accused of breaching.

The 115 charges brought by the Premier League against City included 14 instances of failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

That period covered Mancini's three and a half years in charge, during which he won the FA Cup in 2011 and City's first top-flight title for 44 years in 2012.

Mancini, the current Italy manager, was asked during a news conference before Monday's Nations League game against Turkey about the allegations relating to his remuneration as City manager.

"Found guilty of what?" he said. "It's not an issue that concerns me. It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

" Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

German newspaper Der Spiegel had previously accused City of paying a "significant portion" of Mancini's compensation "by way of a fictitious consultancy contract".

It alleged that Mancini was paid more by City for his role as a consultant to Abu Dhabi club Al Jazira than he was getting from his role as City manager, excluding bonuses and incentives.

On Friday it emerged that an independent panel had found City guilty of all but one count of charges brought against them by the Premier League, although sanctions have yet to be determined.

The Premier League declined to comment, while City released a statement saying the "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality".

It added: "The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Other Premier League clubs are believed to have been informed about the decision and have sought legal advice over possible compensation claims.

City were charged with more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules following a four-year investigation in February 2023.

The club was referred to an independent commission. A behind-closed-doors hearing began in September 2024 and ran for about 12 weeks.

articles.title: La mejoría de sensaciones concede una tregua a Albert Celades
articles.standfirst: El técnico ha reforzado su posición tras la imagen mostrada ante Girona y Tenerife, aunque el Cádiz continúa sin ganar después de siete jornadas
articles.summary: El técnico ha reforzado su posición tras la mejoría mostrada ante Girona y Tenerife, aunque el Cádiz continúa sin ganar después de siete jornadas
articles.body: Los resultados mantienen a Albert Celades bajo presión, aunque la evolución mostrada por el Cádiz en sus dos últimos encuentros ha reforzado provisionalmente la posición del técnico. El conjunto amarillo continúa sin ganar después de siete jornadas y únicamente ha logrado cuatro puntos. El empate en Tenerife no solucionó los problemas clasificatorios, pero confirmó algunos avances. El Cádiz llevó el peso del encuentro durante buena parte de la tarde y dispuso de oportunidades para regresar con un marcador mejor. Sin embargo, una mala salida de balón y la escasa contundencia de David Gil permitieron a Enric Gallego adelantar al cuadro canario. Vladys evitó posteriormente una nueva derrota. La continuidad de Celades había quedado seriamente cuestionada después del partido contra Las Palmas. Más allá de la falta de puntos, preocupaba que el equipo no ofreciera señales de crecimiento. Dentro del club aparecieron partidarios de sustituir al entrenador y comenzaron a estudiarse posibles alternativas para el banquillo. El técnico respondió modificando su planteamiento. El Cádiz ha reducido riesgos, presenta una estructura más equilibrada y trata de aprovechar mejor las características de una plantilla profundamente renovada durante el verano. La derrota frente al Girona ya dejó algunos síntomas positivos y el encuentro de Tenerife confirmó esa tendencia. También empiezan a ganar protagonismo futbolistas como Ibon Sánchez, Vladys, Doué o Manu Fernández, mientras otros jugadores como Izeta, Damián Rodríguez y Jandro Orellana todavía necesitan completar su adaptación. Celades ha conseguido ganar tiempo, pero su margen continúa siendo reducido. La mejoría ha frenado por ahora la posibilidad de un relevo, aunque ese respaldo dependerá de que el Cádiz convierta pronto su evolución futbolística en la primera victoria del curso.

articles.title: Vitor Matos interview: Swansea City boss on their fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool
articles.summary: Vitor Matos speaks to Sky Sports about Swansea City's fast start and working under Jurgen Klopp at Liverpool. Watch Swansea City vs Norwich City live on Sky Sports+ and the Sky Sports app at 12.30pm on Saturday October 10
articles.body:
But Vitor Matos and his high-pressing, energetic side have enjoyed a wonderful opening to the campaign. It is performances, more than results, that have pleased him.

"I'm happy with the start more than the results," Matos - who won Sky Bet Championship Manager of the Month for August - tells Sky Sports .

"It's the style and the feeling that when you go to watch us play, you have a good feeling. We are happy when you are out, especially our fans. That's what we wanted, that's what we are trying more than anything.

Nearly a year since taking the job, and it is clear that Matos has taken to Swansea, and the locals in the city have taken to him. 'The Swansea way' brings connection.

"It's a wonderful place," he says. "It's a strong culture of style as well. That was one of the main reasons I decided to come and one of the main reasons we all felt close to each other.

"We and the owners wanted to bring back and put the team closer to the style it was always recognised for, an offensive one, with the ball, trying to be dominant and aggressive, but at the same time able to compete against every team.

"That is the main part, and having that already as a culture is really good because you can easily connect with each other.

"It's a wonderful place to be. It's a club that you always recognise as a club with a clear identity, with a clear style, which brought the fans together and brought a lot of people together. Being part of that, of course, makes me really proud."

We have seen good starts fall away many a time in the Championship as the hectic nature of the schedule takes its toll.

Matos knows the challenge is maintaining what Swansea do over 46 games.

"It comes a lot with the mindset and the willingness," he says. "When it's part of you, when it's part of your style, when you understand the benefits of that, it's not just because we think it's nice. It's because we really believe it's the best way to win and to compete against all the teams.

"When you start believing in that and make it a proper style and culture of being in the club, then it's possible.

"Of course, it's hard. Of course, you have different oppositions who demand different things sometimes, but the core ideas, the main principles, they need to be there. That's what we try."

It is some of those ideas and principles that were developed by Matos during his time at Liverpool.

He spent five years working under Jurgen Klopp as an elite development coach.

"I was lucky to work with Jurgen for that long," Matos says. "Of course, not only Jurgen, but all the staff at Liverpool. Pep Lijnders and Peter Krawietz, too.

"It shaped me because the opportunity to work with that level of players at a really young age as well, being exposed to the Premier League, the Champions League and the training sessions, the level was so high and so demanding that, of course, it shapes you.

"I learned a lot and I still learn a lot, and that was, of course, one of the main things in my development.

"We had some players on loan in the Championship, and for that I needed to watch them and know them. If I compare, the level has increased in all directions, technically and tactically. The games are much more played in different ways.

Klopp, now in charge of the German national team, is still always available on the end of the phone.

"I have a lot more questions for Jurgen than he has for me!" Matos says with a smile.

"But it's always nice to speak with all of them. We have a really close relationship - it was much more than football and [all the staff at Liverpool] are still close."

Matos left Liverpool in 2024 to join Lijnders as his assistant at RB Salzburg in Germany. That only lasted a few months before Matos returned home to Portugual for his first senior management role, when he took charge at Maritimo last June.

That lasted just five months, when Swansea came calling last November, and he found himself back in English football - albeit in the Welsh part!

"I always had that desire [to return]," he says. "I never really thought about the when or the timing.

"When I grew as a child, all my development as well, I was always so much into the league, into English football, so I always had that inside me. Of course, after working at Liverpool, even more.

"I could not say that I expected one day, or that it was always in my mind that I wanted to be here in one month or in one year. But it was always there.

"When the opportunity came and when the common ideas and the common values clicked with each other, mine, the club's, the owner's, everything clicked. After that, it was quite an easy decision for me."

For such a young manager, Matos speaks with incredible experience. It likely comes from the fact he knew he wanted to be a coach from the age of 15, and has been working at it ever since.

He insists, however, that he doesn't really ever consider how far he's come.

"I really don't think about it on a daily basis," he says. "We live more for the next game, the next training session, the next drill or the next interview. I think that's where we all are as managers.

"I know I'm a young coach and there's still, of course, a lot to live. I'm really happy with all the things that have happened. You always need a little bit of luck in your career, a little bit of luck in your life.

"Arriving healthy at this age, being able to have a family and having the possibility to do a job in this club that I like so much, all of that came into place. I'm more than anything pleased with the journey so far."

And Swansea City are more than pleased with him.

articles.title: Los suspensos de España que no te esperabas
articles.standfirst: Ferrán y Cucurella fueron los dos futbolistas señalados por La Pizarra en el reparto de notas tras el duelo ante Inglaterra en Wembley
articles.summary: Ferrán y Cucurella fueron los dos futbolistas señalados por La Pizarra en el reparto de notas tras el duelo ante Inglaterra en Wembley
articles.body: España volvió a dejar argumentos para el análisis tras su encuentro ante Inglaterra. En La Pizarra de Radio MARCA, Adrián Blanco, Nahuel Miranda y Álex de Llano pusieron nota a algunos de los nombres propios y aspectos más destacados del partido, con Luis de la Fuente y la madurez competitiva de la Selección como grandes triunfadores. En el apartado de los suspensos aparecieron las ocasiones falladas por Ferran Torres y la actuación defensiva de Marc Cucurella. Dos de los aspectos del encuentro que menos convencieron en La Pizarra. "Lo de Ferran fueron dos ocasiones muy claras, ocasiones muy de Ferran que definió muy mal...", explicó Adrián Blanco. "Era un momento ideal...", dejó caer De Llano. "Cucurella estuvo muy separado. Le superan muy fácilmente en la contra del 1-1. Percibí cierta de tensión en el 2-1", analizó Blanco. "Cucurella no está bien, da la sensación de que está poco ágil y que le cuestan los controles. Son síntomas de un futbolista fundido que necesita algo de descanso", añadió Nahuel Miranda. La pareja formada por Pau Cubarsí y Aymeric Laporte se llevó el aprobado. Los dos centrales compartieron el eje de la defensa española y su actuación conjunta consiguió superar el corte establecido por La Pizarra. "Son una garantía competitiva, aunque no estuvieron tan brillantes como en la Copa del Mundo", dijo Adrián. "Con balón estuvieron desacertados, sobre todo Laporte. Era un partido de máxima exigencia donde el equipo tampoco les estaba dando muchos", analizó Nahuel. Un escalón por encima apareció la presión adelantada de la Selección. El trabajo de España sin balón recibió un 'bien' después de un encuentro en el que el equipo también atravesó momentos de menor control. Precisamente, en sus declaraciones posteriores al partido, Mikel Oyarzabal analizó el encuentro: "Hemos entrado bien al partido, aunque se nos ha complicado en los últimos diez o 15 minutos del primer tiempo. Hemos concedido alguna transición en la que nos ha podido hacer daño... pero contentos porque ganar es ganar". Entre los nombres propios mejor valorados estuvo Lamine Yamal. El partido del atacante recibió un notable por parte de La Pizarra. "Hizo el primero estando muy listo y se le vio muy aplicado en defensa", aseguró Adrián. "Fue con el cuchillo entre los dientes, fue a por todo y también a recuperar balones. Tuvo una gran demostración de actitud", añadió Nahuel. La misma calificación obtuvo Álex Baena. "Hizo el gol, se encuentra muy cómodo y en esa zona la controla perfectamente", explicó Adrián. "No es un velocista, no deja rivales atrás, pero puede aportar mucho sumando el pase encontrando a compañeros y sabes que cuando recibe la pelota en el último tercio lo va a gestionar bien. Cuando sale Baena cambia el partido", profundizó De Llano. La máxima nota quedó reservada para dos aspectos. El primero fue la dirección de campo de Luis de la Fuente. "Volvió a acertar con los cambios, en el momento indicado, con las entradas de Oyarzabal, Baena o Pedri. Tuvieron impacto en el juego y en el resultado, que es lo que cuenta", destacó Adrián. El segundo sobresaliente fue para la madurez competitiva de España. "Esto te lo da ganar", resumió Nahuel ante lo que De Llano aseguró que la selección es "capaz de readaptarse a los escenarios en los que se plantea, que se encuentra muy cómoda en cualquier escenario que le plantea el rivel".

articles.title: Two Antigua and Barbuda players sent off for pulling Anguilla player's dreadlocks
articles.summary: Antigua and Barbuda players are red-carded for pulling Anguilla player Aedan Scipio's dreadlocks in a Concacaf Nations League game.
articles.body:
With hair that reaches his ankles, Aedan Scipio's dreadlocks are certainly hard to miss.

In fact, the 36-year-old's hair is so long that he has to wear a band around his waist to keep it tied to his body.

But while the forward's lengthy locks may be his standout feature, they can be somewhat of an operational hazard.

Scipio emerged from the bench in the 69th minute with Anguilla already 5-0 down against Antigua and Barbuda in their Concacaf Nations League game at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium.

It took just three minutes for Scipio to inadvertently make an impact, when opponent Keon Greene was shown a straight red card for tugging his dreadlocks.

Incredibly, the hair-pulling didn't end there.

Antigua and Barbuda were reduced to nine men in added time when Scipio was taken off his feet by Shalon Knight pulling his dreadlocks from behind.

Scipio's Anguilla are 210th in Fifa's international rankings, with San Marino the only nation below them.

articles.title: Camavinga hace autocrítica
articles.standfirst: El francés reconoce que le falta "más consistencia" y "cometer menos fallos" para intentar ganarse la confianza de Mourinho en el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El francés reconoce que le falta "más consistencia" y "cometer menos fallos" para intentar ganarse la confianza de Mourinho en el Real Madrid
articles.body: Eduardo Camavinga afronta su sexta temporada en el Real Madrid y lo hace con muchas incógnitas. Su rendimiento se ha ido apagando paulatinamente y el futbolista es tan consciente que no tiene problemas en hacer autocrítica y trabajar para intentar revertir la situación. El francés, que llegó en 2021 procedente del Rennes previo pago de 40 millones de euros (31 más 9 en variables), está teniendo serios problemas para demostrar por qué era uno de los centrocampistas con mayor proyección del fútbol europeo. No en vano, Deschamps lo dejó fuera del pasado Mundial, algo que dejó muy tocado al jugador. "Perderme el Mundial me afectó. Este tipo de decepción fue algo nuevo para mí, pero lo más importante es levantarse", comentó Camavinga en la previa del partido de este lunes ante Bélgica. Ahí sí estará porque Zidane, nuevo seleccionador francés, ha decidido repescarle para el combinado galo en busca de su mejor versión. "Desde que empezó mi carrera todo ha ido muy rápido, pero Roma no se construyó en un día y todavía tengo mucho tiempo delante", confía el del Real Madrid. Y precisamente es en su club donde debe empezar a mejorar su rendimiento si quiere ganarse un puesto en el once blanco y en el de Francia. El año pasado, con Xabi Alonso y luego Arbeloa en el banquillo, Camavinga fue titular en 16 de los 31 partidos ligueros que estuvo disponible. No tuvo un sitio del todo fijo en el campo y muchas veces señalado por parte de la grada. Ahora, con Mourinho a la batuta, a la situación no parece ir a mejor. En las siete primeras jornadas ha sido titular sólo en dos ocasiones y ante el Elche ni siquiera salió desde el banquillo. El centrocampista es consciente y no duda en hacer autocrítica: "Me falta más consistencia. He tenido buenas actuaciones, pero necesito ser más consistente". Valverde y Tchouaméni gozan de mucha más confianza por parte de Mourinho, algo que Camavinga lucha por intentar cambiar. "Tengo que estar más concentrado en el terreno de juego y cometer menos fallos", reconoció el galo, que ha recuperado la ilusión con Zidane en Francia: "Sólo quiero que me dé confianza. Es muy especial estar a sus órdenes porque todo el mundo sabe lo que significa Zidane en este país".

articles.title: Super League Grand Final 2026: Date, venue, timings as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity look to become sixth-ever winner
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Megan Wellens takes you through everything you need to know as Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity to be crowned champions; watch the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3 from 5pm on Sky Sports
articles.body:
When and where is the 2026 Super League Grand Final?

The Grand Final is taking place on Saturday October 3, 6pm kick-off, live on Sky Sports , with the 'Theatre of Dreams' Old Trafford once again the host venue for the blockbuster event.

Starting back in 1998, the Grand Final has always taken place at the home of Manchester United (barring 2020 at Hull), with 10 different teams having competed for the trophy... so far!

Now that becomes 11 as Wakefield join St Helens, Wigan Warriors, Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos, Hull FC, Catalans Dragons, Salford Red Devils, Castleford Tigers, Warrington Wolves, and Hull KR in experiencing walking out of the tunnel

However, not all these teams have won it.

Indeed, only Wigan, Saints, Bradford, Leeds, and Hull KR have lifted the coveted trophy, with the rest of Super League daring to dream they can one day join that very small list.

We now know that one of Warrington and Wakefield will join those other five. Remarkably, it also marks the first ever Grand Final which has not included one of Wigan, Leeds, or St Helens.

Super League Grand Final teams: Consistency and an underdog mentality

The Super League Grand Final marks a meeting between the two teams who finished third and fourth in the table in 2026 and probably went under the radar more than they should have.

Both teams are packed with stars but only a couple got individual plaudits. Warrington Wolves' loose forward Ben Currie and Wakefield Trinity prop Caleb Hamlin-Uele were included in this year's Dream Team.

Despite that, they both pulled off the ultimate wins to make it to the final as Warrington battled past Leeds and Wakefield annihilated Wigan in one of the biggest semi-final wins ever.

What has made both Warrington and Wakefield so formidable in 2026 is that they play so in sync as a team. Job roles are defined, and they will do absolutely anything for one another, defensively putting their bodies on the line.

Keep your eyes out for Warrington's George Williams and Ewan Irwin bringing the flair, Matty Ashton bringing the pace, and James Bentley, Currie, and James Harrison laying down a marker.

For Wakefield, Tyson Smoothy is the anchor of the ship, with Tom Johnstone a constant threat on the edge, then the likes of Hamlin-Uele, Isaiah Vagana, and Caius Faatili tearing it up the middle.

This is such a tough question to answer in 2026. Warrington beat Wakefield 27-16 all the way back in round 3 but then Wakefield won a hard-fought game 25-18 in round 26.

It is one of those games where you would not be shocked if either team took the victory.

Also at play here is experience. Warrington have not been in a Grand Final since 2018 and Wakefield have never been in one.

However, both teams have big-game players who are going to have to guide them through this moment.

It is for moments like this that Williams was brought to Warrington - he wants to leave with a trophy and this is his final shot.

On the other side, Smoothy won an NRL Grand Final just 12 months ago.

The stage is set for someone to take hold of and own the match.

Four teams have kept a tight grip on the trophy, one joined them last year, and now we know we will get a sixth...

Known as the Harry Sunderland Trophy from 1998 until 2023, the 2024 Grand Final saw the first Rob Burrow Award presented to the player of the match. Bevan French was the inaugural winner after his game-breaking display for Wigan Warriors and Mikey Lewis then picked it up in 2025 for a game of sheer dominance.

It was previously named after Sunderland who was a rugby league administrator both in the UK and Australia but the Rugby Football League Association announced in February that the player of the match award would be renamed to honour the late, great Leeds Rhinos No 7 and MND campaigner.

Burrow was the first player to win the Harry Sunderland Trophy twice and now the award is named after the rugby league legend as a "show of our gratitude to Rob for being the player he was."

The list of winners is littered with big rugby league names and a lot of legends...

Sir Kevin Sinfield has already set off on his final challenge which started at the home of world club champions Hull KR on Sunday September 27 and visits each of the home grounds of the 12 English Super League clubs, before finishing at Old Trafford ahead of the Grand Final on Saturday October 3.

Sinfield, who led Leeds to seven Grand Final glories at the Theatre of Dreams, will present the match ball in readiness for the current-day gladiators to do battle.

Sinfield has helped raise more than £11m for the MND community with his team since his first annual challenge in 2020.

Soul Symphony will provide pre- and half-time entertainment for fans to enjoy and Laura Wright returns to perform a spine-tingling rendition of Jerusalem as is customary before the big dance.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will take place at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Playoff Bracket Projections and Predictions after Week 4
articles.summary: An action-packed Saturday slate has created a fresh outlook for the race to the 2026 season's edition of the College Football Playoff.
articles.body:
An action-packed Saturday slate has created a fresh outlook for the race to the 2026 season's edition of the College Football Playoff.

Florida and Mississippi State both landed marquee wins in Week 4, soaring into the projected CFP field. Florida knocked Ole Miss out of the bracket, while Mississippi State capitalized on a loss elsewhere.

As of now, the SEC dominates the Playoff conversation. But as conference play heats up, there will be plenty of movement—and opportunity for other leagues.

The projected bracket is a reflection of B/R's Top 25 dropped into the organization of the official CFP format.

Immediately after toppling LSU, Ole Miss turned around and lost at Florida. It was a statement victory for the offense-driven Gators, who have rapidly ascended under new coach Jon Sumrall. Florida improved to 4-0, soaring into the projected CFP bracket with an at-large position.

Wake Forest also stunned Louisville, but the most impactful upset of the weekend belonged to Wisconsin. Penn State entered with a 3-0 record, sitting just on the wrong side of the Playoff bubble. However, the Nittany Lions blew a 17-point lead and gave up a 72-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter of this loss.

Oregon 41, USC 27 Mississippi State 31, Missouri 24

Oregon quarterback Dante Moore left with an injury, but USC could not stop Dylan Raiola in a disappointing home loss. Mississippi State, meanwhile, had a dominant fourth quarter to take out Mizzou. As a result, Mississippi State essentially took USC's spot in the latest bracket.

1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Notre Dame 4. Miami 5. Indiana 6. Ohio State 7. Florida 8. Alabama 9. Mississippi State 10. BYU 11. LSU 12. Utah 13. Texas Tech 14. Iowa 15. Ole Miss 16. Duke 17. Virginia Tech 18. Tennessee 19. UCLA 20. USC 21. Oklahoma State 22. Oregon 23. Missouri 24. Cincinnati 25. Boise State

Seeding is a reflection of how B/R's Top 25 would shape the bracket.

Power 4 Champions and Top Group of 6 Team

Highlighted by four games including two Top 25 teams, the SEC provided some nonstop drama on Saturday.

Texas went on the road and edged Tennessee 20-17 behind a five-sack performance from Colin Simmons. Georgia put a 41-13 beatdown on Oklahoma, and Florida had an unstoppable offense in a 52-28 victory over Ole Miss.

During the evening window, Alabama cranked up the heat on Shane Beamer's seat in a 49-18 rout of South Carolina as LSU smoked Texas A&M 35-6 and Mississippi State clipped Mizzou 31-24.

In short: Florida and Mississippi State are feeling really good—joining Texas and Georgia as confident 4-0 teams. LSU avoided a wave of panic with its rout, too.

Ole Miss won't be thrilled with a lopsided result or a struggling defense, but the Rebels are still in decent shape. On the other hand, the vibes are straight-up horrendous at OU, South Carolina and Texas A&M.

Week 4 set the stage for what should be a chaotic season in the SEC.

Speaking of the SEC, the noon window features a massive game between Alabama and Mississippi State—you know, just as we all expected. Even though Bama isn't the class of the conference right now, Mississippi State taking down a brand of that stature would be huge for the program. Alabama, nevertheless, is the favorite for this cowbell-crazed contest in Starkville.

Want to contend nationally? You'd better win on the road. Ohio State and Florida—which are ranked fifth and eighth, respectively, in the updated AP Top 25—are headed to No. 14 Iowa and No. 25 Missouri. If either or both hosts win, the Big Ten and/or SEC standings would get an interesting twist.

Similar story for Miami. On paper, the 'Canes should not come close to losing this matchup. Clemson is 3-1 but hasn't looked dangerous on offense. Still, when top teams are on the road in conference play, strange things are known to happen.

articles.title: Top 8 Overreactions after Week 4 of 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: When we look back at Week 4 months from now, we will remember it as the Saturday that started it all.
articles.body:
When we look back at Week 4 months from now, we will remember it as the Saturday that started it all.

From emerging College Football Playoff contenders to unexpected, Herculean player performances to seismic hot seat changes on the coaching, this weekend overloaded us with important intel that will prove useful in the weeks to come.

Some were positive, many were not. Either way, it's the most telling week of CFB to date.

On paper, it looked like a mammoth weekend of college football. Thankfully, it delivered and then some. It also provided us with plenty to overreact to.

The Deion Sanders Experiment Has Failed at Colorado

It hasn't been boring. That's for certain.

And the highs Sanders brought to Boulder courtesy of his son Shedeur along with Heisman winner Travis Hunter were sensational. For a while, the trajectory at Colorado felt tangible. Those moments were very real.

But as we sit here on the brink of October, with the Buffaloes sitting at 2-2 with three difficult games—Texas Tech, Utah and Oklahoma State—on deck, it's hard not to accept where we are.

In his last 16 games against Power Four teams, Sanders is 3-13. Perhaps more glaring of all, the level of play seems to be rapidly deteriorating. After ugly losses to Northwestern and Baylor this is where we are.

In fact, Sanders is lucky not to be 1-3.

To be clear, this is a difficult job. It's hard to win at Colorado, and Sanders' presence provided this program with a jolt of energy it needed.

But we've seen at schools such as Indiana and UCLA what can be done in a short period of time, and it just doesn't feel like this momentum will change anytime soon.

We know where this is headed unless something changes drastically. The next few weeks likely won't help.

Shane Beamer Will Be Out of a Job Before Thanksgiving

On the topic of coaching turmoil, enter Shane Beamer.

To say the optics of South Carolina's loss to Alabama were less than ideal would be an understatement.

The Gamecocks lost 49-18, although the game actually felt worse than the score indicated. The score was 35-3 before halftime.

Beyond the blowout, which won't sit well with the fanbase, is the exchange Beamer shared with Dylan Stewart, the team's star defensive player. In the exchange , Beamer can be seen yelling at Stewart, although the player doesn't exactly seem engaged in the spirited pep talk.

If we wanted to dedicate a section on how much Stewart hurt his draft stock this week, we could do that as well.

For Beamer, who is coaching for his job, a miracle might be needed. South Carolina plays Kentucky, Florida, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Texas A&M, Arkansas, Georgia and Clemson the rest of the way.

Can he win four of these games to (maybe) save his job? We shall see.

We need some positivity, and Luke Fickell has plenty of it heading into Week 5. That's not exactly something we've said a lot over the past few years, although the progress this season is evident.

In desperate need of, well, anything, Fickell's team delivered a massive comeback win over Penn State in Happy Valley. The team fell behind 17-0 in the first half, and things looked bleak.

With his first-string QB healthy, the Wisconsin offense has some spunk. And while Colton Joseph needs to limit the turnovers, he's provided this team with an edge it has severely lacked.

As for the program, few coaches entered the year on thinner ice. The Badgers chose to keep Fickell and spend around him rather than pay for the buyout.

The team's lone loss came to Notre Dame, and the team battled valiantly early. As for the rest of the schedule, it's suddenly manageable. Games against UCLA, USC and Iowa won't be easy, although the last month has plenty of winnable games.

A nine-win season is within reach, and that should be enough. The importance of what happened against Penn State cannot be overstated. Massive win.

Jeremiah Smith is the Best Player in College Football, and It's Not Close

No debate. No further conversation needed. We could end this section here and move on.

But let's celebrate Smith's Saturday to fully capture what we're witnessing. The Ohio State wide receiver caught 12 passes for 217 yards and four—yes, four—touchdowns against Illinois.

The routes were diabolical, and his hands were insanely strong (per usual). He was the best player on the field. Let's be honest, he's always the best player on the field.

Through four games, Smith has 33 catches for 617 yards and seven touchdowns. He leads the nation in receiving yards, and he's tied for first in touchdowns despite everyone in the stadium knowing he's getting the ball.

In the year of the quarterback, with so much talent at the position, Smith stands alone. Perhaps the more interesting debate at this point, with plenty of games still to play in his CFB career, is where he stacks up against the best wideouts to ever play.

We'll save those declarations for another day. But needless to say, he's entered the conversation.

Dylan Raiola Will Still Be a College Football Superstar

First and foremost, we hope Dante Moore is OK. Oregon's starting QB took a scary hit against USC, and we want him healthy and fully recovered.

As a result of that hit, however, Dylan Raiola, a former 5-star recruit, was thrown into action. The former Nebraska QB didn't just play well; he guided Oregon to a season-saving win on the road against a very capable opponent.

Raiola completed 19 of his 25 throws for 289 yards and two scores. He looked both confident and comfortable. He was smooth under pressure. He was everything the Ducks needed and more.

Coming off a season-ending injury, the thought was that Raiola would sit behind Moore, play during lopsided games here and there, and then be the team's starting QB in 2027.

While Moore's immediate availability remains unknown, it doesn't change how we feel about Raiola. He's immensely talented, and he landed in a situation that seems to suit him well.

Whether he flourishes this year or next, it's a matter of time.

Let's make something abundantly clear. The days of Clemson winning national championships are long gone. The program that conquered Nick Saban and won multiple national championships is no more.

Still, let's give Dabio Swinney some credit. The last six quarters of football have drastically changed the outlook (and vibe) surrounding the program.

In Week 3, the Tigers were in trouble against North Carolina. A prolonged weather delay allowed Clemson to reset, and Swinney's team ultimately prevailed.

On Friday night, Clemson easily handled Cal and one of the most exciting young quarterbacks in college football. The offense remains a work in progress, although the defense seems to be finding its form.

Well, it better be. Clemson plays Miami in Week 5, and the Tigers are an enormous home underdog. While very few expect Clemson to even compete in this game, a solid showing could go a long way.

The good news? After Miami, the schedule eases up quite a bit. If Swinney can keep his team competitive and the offense can find a rhythm, the uneasiness that hovered over this program for weeks could slowly dissipate.

Just think about how ridiculous this would have sounded just a few years ago. The fact that we're doubting Indiana's college football dominance speaks to how unbelievable Curt Cignetti's team has been over the past two years.

Once the doormat of college football, we're now poking holes in the Hoosiers' unbeaten season.

The reality, however, is Indiana's lackluster out-of-conference slate of games has not offered much for us to judge. Against Northwestern in Week 4, the first real test of any kind, the Hoosiers didn't exactly thrive.

Maybe Northwestern is better than we think; maybe Indiana has taken a step back. Maybe, and this feels most likely, both are a bit true.

When you consider how much Indiana lost to the NFL, how could it not take a step back? It wasn't just the departure of Fernando Mendoza, last season's Heisman winner. Cignetti lost impact players on both sides of the ball.

The fact that Indiana is still in this position, ranked in the top 10, speaks to his brilliance.

Still, Indiana isn't the team it once was. That much is clear after this weekend.

That doesn't mean it can't do spectacular things moving forward, although doing so will be significantly more difficult than it once was.

Georgia is the Best Team in College Football

Sure, the schedule has been underwhelming. (Sorry, Oklahoma fans. But this part is true.)

Despite the lack of marquee wins one month into the season, Georgia has that look about it. It's a familiar look, although it's not one we've truly seen for a few seasons.

Through four games, the Bulldogs have outscored opponents 223 to 53. They currently have the No. 1 ranked scoring offense in college football and a defense that ranks in the top 20.

Quarterback Gunner Stockton remains one of the most underappreciated players in the country, and the offense has a sudden abundance of players contributing.

Indeed, other teams vying for CFB's top spot have done more and played better competition. There's no denying that. Even still, the Bulldogs have a roster seemingly constructed for a deep playoff run.

Plus, there will be plenty of time to prove their worth. Games against Alabama, Florida and Ole Miss are on the schedule. Before the regular season is complete, the Bulldogs will have multiple opportunities to showcase just how good they are.

articles.title: Israeli fans direct monkey chants and military slogans at Ireland’s players
articles.summary: Israeli fans directed monkey chants at Ireland’s Adam Idah, who scored a goal in his team’s 3-0 Nations League win.
articles.body:
Israeli supporters have been accused of directing racist chants towards Republic of Ireland player Adam Idah and were filmed raising military slogans during the teams’ UEFA Nations League football match, but have evaded disciplinary action from the competition’s organisers.

Ireland defeated Israel 3-0 in the politically charged encounter at Nagyerdei Stadium in Debrecen, Hungary, with Idah among the goal scorers in the controversial European clash on Sunday.

The 25-year-old Ireland international, born to a Nigerian father and an Irish mother, was targeted with “monkey chants”, as videos circulating on social media showed, but the fans’ behaviour has gone unpunished by UEFA.

An Israeli supporter also led chants about his country’s military from the stands as he attempted to brush aside the team’s drubbing on the football pitch.

Al Jazeera has reached out to European football’s governing body, UEFA, and the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) for comment on the incident and whether the Israeli fans will face any sanctions for their actions.

According to reports in the Irish media, UEFA confirmed that racist abuse by Israeli fans towards Idah occurred, but that the matter cannot be investigated because the protocols were not followed by Irish players and officials.

Ireland midfielder Jayson Molumby, who heard the racist chants before half-time, asked the referee and the fourth official to listen to the alleged monkey chants, an FAI spokesperson was quoted as saying by The Irish Times.

However, a UEFA delegate informed the FAI that an investigation could not be opened as Molumby did not explicitly mention racism to the officials and they had not heard any chanting.

The allegations of racism from Israeli fans came after calls to boycott the match drew international attention.

Youseph Haddad, a member of an Israeli right-wing party, filmed himself in the stands with other supporters as they chanted about the Israeli military amid the team’s abysmal performance on the field.

“Yes, we lose in football, but where we don’t lose,” Haddad says in the video, answering himself: Israeli forces.

“So maybe the football Irish team beat us on the football field, but they will never, ever break the Israeli spirit,” adds Haddad, who is a candidate for the upcoming Israeli parliamentary elections.

It remains unclear whether chanting about the Israeli military would be categorised as “negative behaviour” under UEFA’s rules on spectator behaviour.

According to UEFA’s disciplinary regulations, penalties for national associations whose fans are found guilty of breaking the rules can range from fines to stadium closures and bans on away ticket sales.

However, such sanctions are announced following a disciplinary investigation into the matter.

Al Jazeera has asked UEFA whether the Israel Football Association will face a disciplinary inquiry due to its fans’ sloganeering.

The match itself had been a point of contention for months and on Saturday, the day before the match, it was uncertain whether the game would go ahead, with the FAI and the national team under pressure for months to boycott the fixtures due to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Ireland’s status as a Palestine ally.

But after hours of talks and a vote among the team, the match went ahead, with Ireland players wearing black armbands in support of Palestinians killed during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Irish players also bowed their heads during Israel’s national anthem and did not shake the hands of the Israeli team, while Ireland’s captain, Dara O’Shea, pledged to donate all of his earnings from the match to aid Gaza.

Ireland’s first-choice goalkeeper, Gavin Bazunu , was the only player who publicly opted out of the fixture and posted a statement on social media, saying he felt “it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel”.

Bazunu withdrew from both legs of the fixture, including the next match set to take place on October 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia.

Ireland and Israel are in Group B3 of the ongoing UEFA Nations League.

articles.title: Javier Aguirre: "En un club como el Valencia no puedes deambular por el campo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico mexicano se presenta oficialmente con la idea de ganar cuanto antes: "Basta de mensajes"
articles.summary: El técnico mexicano se presenta oficialmente con la idea de ganar cuanto antes: "Basta de mensajes"
articles.body: Javier Aguirre asume el puesto de entrenador del Valencia con el reto de enderezar a un equipo que ha firmado el peor arranque liguero de su historia reciente y que ocupa la 19ª posición en la tabla con solo cuatro puntos, una victoria, en las siete primeras jornadas de campeonato. Está convencido y así lo demostró durante su presentación oficial en el estadio de Mestalla. El entrenador mexicano, de 67 años, regresa a LaLiga tras sus etapas en Osasuna, Atlético, Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganés y Mallorca. Desde que aterrizó en Osasuna en 2002 se especializó en rescatar a equipos en apuros y consolidarlos en Primera. Ahora, se encontraba sin equipo después de dirigir a la selección de México en el Mundial de 2026. Aguirre llega a Mestalla con un contrato hasta final de temporada, más uno opcional en caso de clasificación para la Europa League (vía Liga). Aun así, el director deportivo, Braulio Vázquez, advirtió que la ampliación del técnico podría no depender de la clasificación: "Podemos quedar el 14º o 15º y renovar a Aguirre porque estemos contentos". El nuevo entrenador blanquinegro tomó las riendas del equipo nada más aterrizar el jueves en la Ciudad Deportiva de Paterna y mantuvo los primeros contactos con la plantilla, con la que aún tiene dos semanas para preparar su primer partido ante el Racing, en el Sardinero. ¿Por qué sí al Valencia? "No le puedo decir que no al Valencia. Nunca, nunca. Es un histórico de la Liga, tiene una afición brutal. Vienes aquí y te acojonas. Y quiero que Mestalla sea un imponente estadio, que le equipo vuelva a los planos en los que merece estar, en los que ha estado a lo largo de su historia. Yo había dejado cuatro ofertas a un lado. Estaba con mi familia, con mi mujer, Silvia con mis nietos. Y le dije: "Silvia, lo siento, pero nos tenemos que ir para allá". ¿Cree que el Valencia está capacitado para ir a Europa' "Soy muy malo para imaginar cosas. Lo que diga el papelito (contrato) no me dice mucho. Si estamos cómodos todos, seguiremos y si no estamos, cómodos no seguiremos". Responsabilidad en el proyecto. "La gente me da la bienvenida. Y notas que hay una atmósfera positiva. Pero esto cuenta de resultados. Esperemos que lleguen lo antes posible. Jugadores que necesita el equipo. "Lo primero que veo es que hay muchos lesionados y eso es lo que me ocupa de momento. Tenemos que recuperarlos, que cambien esa cara. No tengo bien diagnosticado, cómo está el equipo. Yo soy empleado del club, no manejo presupuesto, ni dinero. Eric es amigo, pero no te puedo concretar". Condiciones para que esté aquí: "Condiciones puse pocas. Felicité a Óscar por lo que hizo con el equipo. Por su atrevimiento. Vi la irrupción de Otorbi, de Mayol, no miro la edad. Si el jugador vale, para adelante. Llegué a Espanyol y estaba lleno de jovencitos, pero recurrí a cuatro veteranos salvamos al equipo. Ahora quedan 31 partidos. Van a jugar los que mejor estén". Qué mensaje le da a la afición: "La gente está cansada de mensajes. Basta de mensajes. Vamos a jugar contra el Racing. Vamos a intentar lograr una victoria, lo antes posible. Ese es el mejor mensaje". Mestalla y la desconexión de la afición y si es un entrenador ofensivo o defensivo: "Por supuesto que sé dónde vengo. El plan es ganar, claro. Pero de la mejor forma, la que nos lleve. Me tengo que dedicar lo antes posible a dar una alegría. No sé si soy defensivo más o menos. Si tengo que poner un 1-5-4-1 dependerá. Eso te lo pedirá el partido, el rival". ¿Qué aspectos ve en la plantilla? "Veo mucho talento individual, mucha cantera y de mucha calidad. Y lo único que hay que hacer es convencerlos de que se crean importantes, de que están en una institución que se crea importante. Con una institución de la historia de este club no puedes deambular en el campo. Tienes que dar confianza y que se la crean ellos. El diagnóstico rápido es que falta confianza". Cómo han sido los días de conversación con Rafa Márquez: "La selección mexicana está en muy buenas manos. A Rafa le digo que cuente conmigo para lo que necesite". Mensaje a los jugadores: "Al jugador no le mientas nunca. Dile siempre la verdad. Del futbolista me gusta saber sus orígenes, preguntar. De momento intento ganarme la confianza, generarles al menos el beneficio de la duda. Hago mis anotaciones. A nivel individual he tenido acercamientos con varios, de aquí a Santander espero hablar con todos". ¿Es usted un motivador nato, cómo hace para levantar equipos? "Me preocupan los jugadores que no juegan. Y tienes que estar cerca de ellos, porque en algún momento los vas a necesitar. A todos nos interesa que el Valencia tenga un buen año". Dificultad de la Liga: "Es una carrera larga, la Liga. Es muy complicada". Qué traslada a los jugadores nada más aterrizar: "Esa primera observación de los jugadores, eso me permite a mí. No lo traigo preparado. Apenas viéndolos cuál puede ser útil. Pocas palabras. Dejarlos que fluyan, no hay mucho en la pizarra. Lo que menos necesitan es información que les pueda saturar. Y ves la tabla de clasificación y dices uf, uf, dejarles un fin de semana libre, volver a trabajar. Que tengan opción de respirar también". Cómo espera que la gente reconozca a su equipo: "No entiendo el fútbol si no hay entrega. Si ves un jugador pasivo, tienes que hacer que reaccione. Yo era un futbolista bastante torpe, pero no me ganaba nadie en darlo todo. La entrega no es negociable". ¿Qué peso tiene llevar la camiseta del Valencia? "Más que peso es un orgullo. Estar aquí, en una gran entidad. Cualquiera quisiera estar aquí en mi sitio en este momento. Es un buen reto personal, para el cual me siento preparado". Dijo que este era un buen año de colofón. "No, no dije un año. Un colofón puede ser de 14 años. Aguirre puede hablar y decir, pero si no gano, es la misma historia. Vengo a hablar porque es obligatorio, me obligan. Pero no hubiera venido. Donde hay que hablar es en el campo". Cómo fue la charla con Silvia [esposa de Javier Aguirre] cuando tuvo la propuesta: "A Silvia le gusta más el fútbol que a mí. Nos pilló en un viaje. Va a ser su cumple y no voy a estar. Me dijo de todo, pero está contenta porque estoy trabajando. Sabe lo que me gusta trabajar y lo que me gusta trabajar en España". ¿Les pesa a los jugadores esta camiseta? "Es una buena pregunta. Son seres humanos, no les gustan los insultos. Intentaré canalizar el peso de la camiseta y que sea un orgullo jugar aquí, en el Valencia. Tiene que ser algo natural, como ha sido siempre. Ganar aquí siempre ha sido muy complicado". Necesidades del equipo: "No hemos hablado. Braulio está trabajando. Sé que hay tres centrales lesionados, pero ya es un tema que no me compete a mí hablar con Braulio de posibles fichajes. Llegará un día en que tocará cruzar líneas y hablar. Soy una persona consciente, no soy de decir: 'Si no viene Pedro, Juan, me voy'. La clave está en recuperarlos pronto". ¿Cuál es el objetivo? "No tenía ni idea de que el fair play financiero era el octavo. Mi objetivo es Racing. Sé que no es la mejor respuesta para dar un titular". ¿Le faltaba al Valencia en su carrera? "Me gustaría sentir el volcán de Mestalla, pero a favor mío. Vas al estadio con mucha ilusión y con esa ilusión quieres volver a casa". ¿Ha hablado con Kiat Lim? "Nos hemos hablado a través de una pantalla, nos hemos saludado

articles.title: Israel v Republic of Ireland: FAI investigating alleged racist abuse of Adam Idah
articles.summary: The FAI is amassing high-quality footage of the alleged incident with the aim of presenting evidence to Uefa.
articles.body:
The Football Association of Ireland is investigating whether forward Adam Idah was racially abused by Israel supporters during Sunday's 3-0 Uefa Nations League victory for the Republic of Ireland.

BBC Sport understands that midfielder Jayson Molumby spoke to the match officials during play, asking them to listen out for what he believed to be abusive chanting coming from some of the small number of Israel fans present at the match.

After full-time the officials informed FAI staff members that they did not subsequently hear any racist chanting.

When the FAI spoke to the Uefa match delegate about the alleged incident, they were informed that because no clear allegation of racism was reported during the game, the normal protocols had not been followed and a Uefa investigation could not take place.

The FAI is now conducting its own investigation by amassing high-quality footage of the match, including audio from pitchside microphones, in order to establish whether or not abuse was directed at Idah.

A panel is being set up by the FAI to analyse the footage and audio recordings. If the panel believes there is evidence to suggest Idah was abused, it will make a complaint to Uefa and request a further investigation by European football's governing body.

Idah was unaware of any possible abuse during the match and is now being supported by team-mates and staff members before the Republic of Ireland's remaining three fixtures in the current international break.

It is unclear whether the FAI would present its case to Uefa before or after Sunday's behind-closed-doors game against Israel in Backa Topola, Serbia.

BBC Sport has contacted Uefa for comment.

Republic of Ireland 'raised awareness worldwide' in Israel game

FAI unclear over possible sanctions if game not played

Republic of Ireland defeat Israel in Debrecen

Swansea City player Idah scored the second goal in a match which had been in doubt in the run-up to kick off, amid widespread protests against facing Israel from Irish fans and politicians, and late discussions among the playing squad about whether or not to fulfil the fixture.

The game was held in the city of Debrecen, Hungary, with about 300 Israel supporters present and no tickets sold to Irish fans, though a handful did manage to enter the stadium

The second fixture in Serbia this Sunday is a 'home' match for the Republic of Ireland but has been moved to a remote corner of Europe amid ongoing protests from fans over the FAI's decision to fulfil the fixtures.

The FAI voted earlier this year to play the matches, having been concerned about potential sanctions, including fines and expulsions from competitions, if it had opted to boycott.

Ireland has been among the European countries to most keenly show support for Palestinians since the start of Israel's military offensive in Gaza in October 2023.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

The FAI has asked Uefa to keep the Republic of Ireland and Israel apart in future draws.

'The Irish hate us - we don't like them'

The two teams did not shake hands or exchange pennants before the match kicked off, and the Irish team bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem.

After scoring the third goal, winger Jack Moylan held up and kissed a black armband the Republic of Ireland players were wearing "in recognition of all lives lost in the conflict".

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad following a long meeting held in the hotel, when the match appeared to be in jeopardy as training and the pre-match news conference were repeatedly delayed.

Bazunu said in a statement on social media: "I am a man of strong faith, and try my best to be a person of character and principle. Therefore I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel."

Bazunu has returned to the squad for Thursday's match against Austria in Dublin, but will be absent again for the second game against Israel.

Israel captain Manor Solomon said: "I'm waiting for the next game against them - it will be a completely different game entirely.

"They don't interest me. We have a country 10 times better than theirs - stronger, an amazing country with amazing people.

"We are proud to wear the team shirt and to be Israelis. We are proud of our state and of our soldiers.

"They can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case.

"If I say what I think of them, I would likely be suspended for a few matches. Obviously they hate us. We don't like them."

articles.title: Irish national soccer team should be ashamed for not shaking hands with Israeli opponents
articles.summary: Ireland's soccer players refused to shake hands with Israeli opponents before their Nations League match, sparking fierce debate over the protest.
articles.body: Irish national soccer team players bowed their heads in protest Sunday. They should be hanging their heads in shame. This is a country known for its love of throwing a few back when the moment strikes. But it's disconcerting to see that their drink of choice is the Kool-Aid. The Irish soccer team had faced pressure to boycott Sunday's game against Israel due to the country's response to the Hamas terror attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, which killed nearly 1,200 Israelis. The narrative pushed by much of the media is that the counter-attacks have been akin to a "genocide," which has no basis in reality. Nevertheless, the Irish soccer team has seemed to deem Israel the villain in this conflict, and took out their resentment on the Israeli players. They wouldn't even shake their hands??? Pathetic. ISRAELI OFFICIAL SAYS EU SANCTIONS REVEAL ANTISEMITISM HIDING BEHIND 'SOCIALLY ACCEPTABLE MASK' Let's pretend for a second that Israel was, indeed, the "bad guy" in this conflict — something I don't believe to be true. Does that mean it's OK to shun the athletes representing the country? Where else could you apply that logic? Should opponents of North Korea's teams refuse to shake their players' hands because of a brutal dictatorship responsible for an innumerable amount of human rights abuses? Should opponents of Russian teams refuse to shake their players' hands because of Vladimir Putin's government invading Ukraine? I didn't see Egyptians deny handshakes with Iranian players due to their government's extermination of protesters against the Tehran regime. I never saw players at the World Baseball Classic snub the Venezuelans because of Nicolás Maduro's brutal regime, either. I could go on and on. The world is brutal. Conflict is everywhere. But there's a big difference between protesting a country's government and treating players from said country as pariahs. The Irish soccer team doesn't seem to understand that. Never mind that Israel's attacks have essentially always been in response to attacks brought upon its country. Innocent people die tragically because Hamas uses them as human shields, embedding its fighters and military infrastructure among civilians in schools, hospitals and residential areas. The Israeli government regularly gives warnings that these attacks are coming, and provides aid to the Palestinian people. This is lost on much of the media and artists such as Macklemore, who falsely decry an attempt at "genocide." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But that's neither here nor there in regard to the Israeli soccer players. They are athletes, not politicians. They don't dictate what their government leaders do. The Irish soccer team's players slighting them is a misguided attempt to make themselves look heroic. In fact, they look foolish. Politics are messy. Sports are supposed to be an escape from them. articles.standfirst: Aragón TV ha publicado un vídeo en exclusiva donde se ve que el balón entra por completo
articles.summary: Aragón TV ha publicado un vídeo en exclusiva donde se ve que el balón entra por completo
articles.body: El primer derbi aragonés de la temporada dejó un empate muy polémico entre el Teruel y el Huesca. Si ya había quejas oscenses con el primer tanto local por una supuesta mano en el control, lo que sucedió en la última jugada provocó un enfado mucho mayor. Y es que, Juárez marcó un gol fantasma que el colegiado no dio en directo ni tampoco tras revisarlo en el VAR. Realmente, con las imágenes que le mostraron al árbitro no se podía saber al 100% que el balón había entrado, aunque se podía intuir. Sin embargo, Aragón TV ha publicado en exclusiva un nuevo vídeo que confirma que el esférico y su esfera rebasaron la línea por completa, por lo que tenía razón el Huesca. Un duro golpe para los azulgranas que necesitaban la victoria con urgencia. Ese tanto hubiera roto una dinámica de cuatro jornadas sin triunfos y que ya tenía en entredicho a Raúl Jardiel. Y es que, el Huesca es uno de los candidatos al ascenso y apenas suma seis puntos en cinco partidos. Así había valorado el técnico lo sucedido: "Esas jugadas son de línea, si el línea ve gol tiene que cantar gol. Lo que no hay que hacer es parar el partido y ver el VAR para ver si se ve claro. El árbitro se tiene que mojar y luego si hay revisión pues se revisa. No puedo asegurar que sea gol, no la he visto bien. Es una cosa nueva que a veces los entrenadores no tenemos claro cómo funciona".

articles.title: Vozinha: Cape Verde goalkeeper on fame and fans
articles.summary: Cape Verde's World Cup hero Vozinha says he craves the "peace and tranquillity" of the life he led before he shot to fame.
articles.body:
Cape Verde's heroic World Cup goalkeeper Vozinha says he craves the "peace and tranquillity" of the life he led before he shot to fame.

The 40-year-old shot to global prominence in June when he almost single-handedly kept Spain at bay as Cape Verde drew 0-0 with the European champions on their World Cup debut.

Vozinha's follower count on social media sky-rocketed over the course of the game, from about 50,000 to more than one million.

But his fame shot up even further when Argentina needed extra time to beat Cape Verde in the round of 32.

Vozinha says his life was easier before his World Cup heroics.

"I've lost my peace and tranquillity," he told the Observer. , external

"I no longer have any privacy, or at least much less than I used to.

"Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there's always someone who wants to take a photo with me or asks me for an autograph. Or, worse, someone is filming me.

"That's what has changed most in my life, and I don't think there's anything I can do about it."

Vozinha's mother became part of the fairytale too. After he revealed that she had could not afford a visa to watch his World Cup debut, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced that the visa fee had been waived.

Now Vozinha has revealed that his mother is visited on a daily basis by fans wanting to talk or to take photographs with him.

"A lot of people want to be famous and have a public profile, but they only see the positive side of that reality," said Vozinha.

"To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I'd choose the one I had before."

His World Cup performances for Cape Verde, a West African island nation with a population of 525,000, earned Vozinha a nomination for men's goalkeeper of the year at the Ballon d'Or awards.

"It's nice to feel like a kind of ambassador, but I want to make it clear that what we achieved was a collective effort," Vozinha said.

"We made history and the best news would be if we could harness that momentum to develop our country and improve the living conditions of our people."

articles.title: Rodrygo, cada vez más cerca
articles.standfirst: El brasileño tocó balón por primera vez en Valdebebas, un paso más en su recuperación de la rotura de cruzado y menisco del pasado marzo; su vuelta sigue prevista entre diciembre y enero
articles.summary: El brasileño tocó balón por primera vez en Valdebebas, un paso más en su recuperación de la rotura de cruzado y menisco del pasado marzo; su vuelta sigue prevista entre diciembre y enero
articles.body: Rodrygo Goes dio este lunes uno de los pasos más esperados de su calvario particular. El brasileño volvió a acariciar el balón en Valdebebas, un gesto en apariencia rutinario que, para quien lleva más de medio año alejado del césped, sabe a gran acontecimiento. Fue el último peldaño de una escalera que el extremo sube con paciencia desde el pasado invierno, y que empieza, por fin, a vislumbrar su final. Para entender la magnitud del momento hay que remontarse a aquella fatídica noche del 2 de marzo. Ante el Getafe, en el Bernabéu, todo se le nubló al brasileño en una acción desgraciada que le cambió la temporada. El diagnóstico, demoledor. Rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior y del menisco externo de la rodilla derecha, la lesión más grave de su carrera. Un mazazo que lo apartó del tramo decisivo del curso pasado y, con especial crueldad, del Mundial que soñaba disputar con Brasil a las órdenes de Carlo Ancelotti. El 10 de marzo pasó por el quirófano, y con la operación arrancó una travesía de paciencia estimada para ocho o nueve meses de rehabilitación. Desde entonces, Rodrygo ha ido quemando etapas sin prisa pero sin pausa, consciente de que en las lesiones de este calibre las prisas son malas consejeras. El club, de hecho, ha marcado el ritmo con mano firme, decidido a no acelerar un solo día los plazos. El primer gran hito llegó a comienzos de septiembre, cuando el brasileño reapareció sobre el césped de la Ciudad Deportiva para realizar carrera continua al margen del grupo. "¡Qué buena sensación volver a correr en el campo!", celebró entonces en sus redes, con la ilusión del que atisba la luz al final del túnel. De aquel trote controlado al balón de hoy median semanas de trabajo. Ahora, con el cuero de nuevo en sus botas, Rodrygo encara la recta final de un proceso cuya meta sigue fijada entre diciembre y enero. Aún queda camino, el más delicado quizá, el de recuperar las sensaciones, el ritmo de competición y la confianza plena en una rodilla que hubo que reconstruir. De cerca sigue su evolución Carlo Ancelotti, que el mes pasado se acercó a Valdebebas para interesarse por su estado y el del resto de brasileños, consciente de que el brasileño es una pieza que también entra en sus planes con la selección. Pero el peor tramo ya ha quedado atrás, y Rodrygo se acerca poco a poco al reencuentro con un equipo que, entre tanto, ha cambiado de piel. Porque la lesión le ha privado de algo más que de jugar: no ha podido ponerse aún a las órdenes de Mourinho, que todavía no ha dirigido a un Rodrygo sano y que ni siquiera pudo contar con él en la pretemporada. No es Rodrygo, además, el único que empieza a ver la luz en una enfermería que poco a poco se vacía. Éder Militao, otro de los brasileños de largo recorrido, ya trota junto a sus compañeros y recibió la semana pasada la visita en Valdebebas del equipo médico que lo operó en Finlandia, señal de que su vuelta está más cerca que nunca. También Ferland Mendy avanza en su puesta a punto y se le ve tocando balón. Tres regresos escalonados que, uno tras otro, devolverán a Mourinho unos efectivos que la mala fortuna le ha negado durante buena parte de este arranque de curso.

articles.title: England defenders Ezri Konsa and Nico O'Reilly doubts to face Czech Republic
articles.summary: Ezri Konsa and Nico O'Reilly are both doubts to play in England's Nations League match against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
Ezri Konsa and Nico O'Reilly are both doubts to play in England's Nations League match against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night.

The pair were the only two members of the England squad to miss training on Monday morning, with the players following their own individual programmes.

Both played the full 90 minutes in England's 3-2 loss to Spain on Saturday.

Manchester City's O'Reilly started at left-back, a position he made his own during the World Cup, and his absence would open an opportunity for Lewis Hall to play.

It was O'Reilly's mistake which led to Alex Baena drawing Spain level at 2-2 at Wembley before the World Cup winners went on to claim victory.

Arsenal centre-back Konsa has become one of Tuchel's most trusted players and started seven of the eight matches at the World Cup.

Central defender Jarrad Branthwaite came on for Marc Guehi late on against Spain and could be a contender to start if Konsa is unavailable.

England play four matches in this international window and, after the loss to Spain, take on the Czech Republic both home and away, either side of travelling to Rijeka to play Croatia.

articles.title: La Uruguay de Forlán desborda a Robert Moreno y Kang in Lee
articles.summary: Darwin brilló con un doblete
articles.body: Entusiasmada Corea del Sur con el 3-0 a Ecuador en el estreno de Robert Moreno, la selección de Uruguay la devolvió a la tierra con una goleada incontestable en Seúl, desbordada por la pegada del conjunto celeste, con tres goles en la primera parte y un 'doblete' de Darwin Núñez, ante Kang in Lee y compañía. En 43 minutos, el 0-3 era una expresión nítida de la efectividad del conjunto celeste, que jugó a lo que se propuso desde el banquillo de Forlán, con su presión arriba, con su firmeza defensiva, con su intención de salir con el balón jugado y con verticalidad. Sabe lo que quiere su nuevo entrenador. Y se añadió lo más fundamental de todo: acertó sobre la portería contraria, quizá por la inspiración en el banquillo por un goleador de una dimensión tan enorme como Forlán. Comedido en la celebración del 0-1 de Darwin Núñez en el minuto 13, el seleccionador se liberó más con el 0-2 de De Arrascaeta, figura del encuentro y finalmente lesionado en el 77. El 0-3 promovido por Guillermo Varela sentenció la primera victoria del legendario goleador al frente de la Celeste, tras el fiasco del Mundial 2026. En el estreno cayó 3-1 con Japón. Su triunfo este lunes fue un alivio. Uruguay no había ganado ni un solo partido en este año, con cuatro empates y dos derrotas. Es más, su última victoria se remontaba más allá, a hace ocho encuentros, cuando se impuso a Uzbekistán por 1-2. Fue hace casi un año. El 13 de octubre de 2025. Con Kang in Lee de vuelta al once titular (en el anterior amistoso descansó y no disputó ni un solo minuto con la carga de partidos con el Atlético de Madrid) y con Son Heung Min de nuevo en el ataque, no fue suficiente para el conjunto surcoreano, que sufrió la pegada de su adversario en la primera parte y reaccionó en la segunda, pero sin el acierto necesario.

articles.title: Who should be the Happy State Bank High School Athlete of the Week?
articles.summary: Athletes from Randall, Highland Park, Gruver, Canyon, Palo Duro, Amarillo High, West Plains and Spearman are among this week's nominees.
articles.body:
Fall sports are in full swing, with football, volleyball and cross country seasons underway.

Standouts from each sport are among this week's nominees for the Happy State Bank High School Athlete of the Week.

The Globe-News is taking weekly nominations and will release a list of finalists for the Happy State Bank High School Athlete of the Week each week.

Students in all varsity sports are eligible to be nominated. The poll will close noon Thursday and the winners will be announced thereafter.

Nominations are due by 5 p.m. each Saturday and can be submitted through email at sports@amarillo.com.

Please include statistics from the week's games and any pertinent information or honors.

Take a look at this week's candidates and cast your vote.

Chloe Brown, Randall volleyball — Brown notched 14 digs, seven aces, five kills and three assists in a win against Borger as well as 12 kills, 9 digs and two aces in a win against Hereford.

Kaitlin Lucas, Highland Park volleyball — Lucas logged 29 assists and 10 digs in a win against Abernathy.

Jett Pittman, Gruver football — Pittman went 13-of-24 through the air, throwing for 335 yards and six touchdowns while adding another score on the ground in the Greyhounds' win against Wellington.

Presli Pool, Canyon girls cross country — Pool won the Canyon Invitational cross country meet with a time of 16 minutes, 42.07 seconds, leading Canyon to a first-place finish in the team standings.

Julian Reese II, Palo Duro football — Reese went 14-of-24 through the air, throwing for 192 yards and two touchdowns while adding 10 carries for 143 yards and three scores on the ground in a win against Wichita Falls Legacy.

Sy Richardson, Amarillo High football — Richardson ran for 289 yards and three touchdowns on 23 carries in the Sandies' win against Frenship Memorial, adding one catch for five yards.

Idaly Sotelo, West Plains volleyball — Sotelo tallied 18 digs and two aces in a win against Perryton and 34 digs in a win against Hereford.

Jailen Vasquez, Spearman football — Vasquez went 10-of-12 through the air, throwing for 130 yards and two touchdowns while adding 113 yards rushing and three more scores on the ground in a win against Abernathy.

Submit nominees, with stats, honors and accolades from the previous week by Saturday each week to sports@amarillo.com

articles.title: El gol más especial de Dani Güiza
articles.standfirst: A sus 46 años, el delantero del Trebujena CF dedicó el gol a sus padres fallecidos
articles.summary: A sus 46 años, el delantero del Trebujena CF dedicó el gol a sus padres fallecidos
articles.body: Dani Güiza ha marcado en su dilatada carrera goles de todos los colores, pero seguro que ninguno tan especial como el que marcó el pasado domingo. El delantero anotó para su nuevo equipo, el Trebujena CF, y no dudó en dedicárselo a sus padres, fallecidos en los últimos meses. El jugador, de 46 años, salió en la segunda parte ante el CD El Torno, que iba ganando en ese momento 1-0. Güiza saltó al campo y en pocos minutos logró la igualada tras un gran remate de cabeza den plancha a centro lateral. Luego su equipo lograría el segundo y así certificaba el triunfo. Pero la imagen del encuentro estuvo en la celebración del veterano futbolista. Nada más anotar, Güiza miró al cielo y señaló con los dedos en una clara dedicatoria hacia sus padres, fallecidos en los últimos meses. "Mamá, Papá, este gol va por vosotros. Gracias por haberme cuidado tan bien. Os quiero con locura y nunca os voy a olvidar. Os amo", escribió el jugador en sus redes sociales.

articles.title: England Women name 2026 Rugby League World Cup squad with four potential debutants included
articles.summary: The Rugby League World Cup takes place from October 15 until the final on November 15; Nine players have been selected from Wigan Warriors; NRLW Grand Finalist Jasmin Strange is included and eligible through her English-born mother
articles.body:
Four potential debutants have made the cut, including NRLW Grand Finalist Jasmin Strange. The 23-year-old Australia- born second-rower, who qualifies through her English-born mother, will link up with the England squad in Perth after the Roosters face Brisbane Broncos on Sunday October 4.

The other uncapped players named in the squad are Connie Boyd (Leeds Rhinos), Hope Millard (Canterbury Bulldogs) and Lucie Sams (Wigan Warriors).

All three nominees for this year's Woman of Steel Award have been selected, alongside six of their Wigan Warriors team-mates. Jenna Foubister, Eva Hunter and Megan Williams will discover who has been crowned this season's outstanding player on Tuesday September 29 before flying to Australia next Thursday.

Fran Goldthorp will represent England for the first time since the 2022 World Cup, where she made four appearances and scored three tries. She is selected alongside two other England players based in the NRLW: Georgia Roche (Newcastle Knights) and Hollie-Mae Dodd (Canberra Raiders).

The newly-crowned Betfred Women's Super League champions York Valkyrie are represented by Liv Wood, while the competition's leading try-scorer, Amelia Brown (Huddersfield Giants), is also included.

St Helens loose forward Jodie Cunningham is joined in the squad by team-mate Vicky Whitfield, with the 34-year-old set to feature at her fourth World Cup.

There are five Leeds Rhinos players, with Young Player of the Year nominees Boyd and Ruby Bruce both recognised for their efforts this season with a place.

Head coach Barrow, said: "The standard across the wider group has been outstanding throughout the season, which made the selection process incredibly challenging.

"At the start of the year, we set out a clear selection timeline with the players, outlining the standards, milestones and opportunities that would contribute to today's selection. Throughout the season, we've had a number of England camps, we have travelled to France, and I've been present at all the Super Four games to assess the players in contention for selection.

"Narrowing our squad from 40 players to a final 23 has involved some difficult decisions, but we believe we have the right balance of experience and youth to compete on the world stage.

"It's also an exciting moment for the programme with the inclusion of Australian-based heritage players for the first time. Bringing together talent from both the NRLW and the Women's Super League gives us a unique blend of quality and experience, and we're excited to see these players come together in an England shirt.

"Now our focus turns to preparation. We know the challenges that await at a World Cup, but we are travelling with a squad that believes in itself, embraces the responsibility of representing England, and is determined to make the nation proud."
